## Source: 03_Data_and_Code/mHealth/recurring_examples/results/VISUALIZATION.md

# mHealth Visualization Examples

The examples compare recording behavior in May and June 2016 for the 340 teaching-cohort users with a food entry before May 1. Membership is fixed before the comparison. The source checksum is recorded in [visualization.json](visualization.json); cohort preparation and source definitions are in the [example guide](../README.md) and [data dictionary](../../DATA_DICTIONARY.md).

## Reproduce

Use the pinned [requirements](../requirements.txt). From the repository root:

```sh
python 03_Data_and_Code/mHealth/recurring_examples/visualization.py
python 03_Data_and_Code/mHealth/recurring_examples/visualization_charts.py
python 03_Data_and_Code/mHealth/recurring_examples/chart_assessment.py
python 03_Data_and_Code/mHealth/recurring_examples/test_visualization.py
```

The first command loads the existing public teaching-data release and cohort cache. Download instructions are in the parent guide. The next command creates three editable TikZ figures in `06_Lecture_Notes/figures` and the browser chart. `06_Lecture_Notes/build_notes.py --figures` compiles the notes and updates figure PNG previews when Pandoc, Tectonic, Poppler, and Pillow are available. Complete program text is printed in M2, Sections 2.14–2.15, and M8, Section 8.12. M3, Section 3.6.1, interprets the paired interval.

## Files and Variables

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| [visualization.json](visualization.json) | Membership, source checksum, monthly aggregates, bootstrap seed/draws, paired change, intervals, and individual-change quantiles. |
| [visualization_monthly.csv](visualization_monthly.csv) | Two rows, one per month. Counts, calendar denominators, logging percentages, and entries per recorded day. |
| [visualization_ecdf.csv](visualization_ecdf.csv) | Aggregate frequency at each distinct logging fraction, with the exact cumulative percentage and eligible-user count. |
| [visualization_interactive.html](visualization_interactive.html) | Month selector, denominator comparison, distribution plot, and visible aggregate table. Download and open locally, or serve as a static HTML file. GitHub's repository file view displays source. |
| [visualization_interactive.vl.json](visualization_interactive.vl.json) | Machine-readable Vega-Lite specification and embedded aggregate data. |
| [chart_assessment.json](chart_assessment.json) | Outcomes for the correct specification and four constructed chart mistakes. |

`observed_user_days` counts distinct user/date pairs with at least one food entry. `calendar_user_days` equals the fixed eligible-user count times the month's calendar length. `logger_calendar_days` instead uses only users with at least one log that month. `logging_percent` and `conditional_logging_percent` use those respective denominators. `entries_per_observed_day` divides all recorded food rows by observed user-days.

The distribution's `logging_percent` is an individual user's fraction of calendar days with logs, expressed as a percentage. `users_at_value` is the aggregate count at that value; `cumulative_percent` is the percentage of eligible users at or below it. Ties and zeros remain in the table. No user identifiers or individual histories are exported by these programs.

## Interpretation

May and June logging coverage is 67.19% and 62.07% for the fixed population, compared with 72.07% and 67.42% when conditioning on a user logging that month. Mean entries per observed day are 11.80 and 11.69. The difference between conditional intensity and population coverage matters for a retention decision.

The paired change is -5.12 percentage points, with a 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of [-7.93, -2.43], using 5,000 resamples and seed 534. The bootstrap resamples whole users with both monthly outcomes together. It assumes independent users under an empirical user-history sampling model with the months fixed. Shared calendar shocks and population representativeness are outside that model. The separately labeled independent-day interval is deliberately incorrect for the observed dependence structure.

The distribution plot describes customer heterogeneity; the interval plot describes uncertainty about the average change. Neither comparison estimates the effect of a product intervention. A day with no food entry is zero for observed logging, while consumption on that day remains unobserved.

## Figure Descriptions

- **Denominators:** grouped May/June bars start at zero. Illinois Blue uses all eligible calendar user-days; Illini Orange conditions on users with logs in each month. Identical numerators produce different percentages.
- **Distribution:** solid blue May and dashed orange June step curves show the percentage of eligible users at or below each logging fraction. Endpoint masses at zero and daily recording remain visible.
- **Uncertainty:** both horizontal intervals center on the same mean change. The paired-user interval is wider than the incorrect independent-day interval; a dashed vertical line marks zero change.

The browser chart preserves 0–100% scales for both month selections, reports counts in tooltips, and supplies a static table. Its JavaScript libraries load from a CDN, so chart rendering requires internet access; the table remains available offline. No Python server or external AI service is used by the exported page.

## Verification

The three programs were executed locally with Python 3.13, pandas 2.2.3, numpy 2.1.3, and Altair 5.5.0. Five independent tests cover calendar lengths, duplicate dates, empty months, tied CDF values, preserved pairs, and constructed unit/denominator/baseline errors. The chart assessment accepts the correct specification and rejects each constructed mistake; this is not a measured error rate for an LLM.

The PDF and all three TikZ previews were compiled and visually reviewed. Browser interaction testing was unavailable because the desktop was locked; both month parameter states were independently compiled and rendered with Vega-Lite 5.20, with rendered labels checked against the numerical evidence. The validation record is [visualization_validation.json](visualization_validation.json). Downloaded reference notebooks were inspected as sources and were not executed.

## Sources

Chart choice draws on the [Financial Times Visual Vocabulary](https://github.com/Financial-Times/chart-doctor/blob/main/visual-vocabulary/README.md). Distribution and uncertainty distinctions are supported by the [seaborn tutorials](https://seaborn.pydata.org/tutorial.html). The [Altair tutorial](https://github.com/altair-viz/altair-tutorial) supplies the declarative-interaction approach; the course programs use their own mHealth transformations and current pinned syntax. [VisEval](https://github.com/microsoft/VisEval) motivates the distinction among executable code, fidelity to a request, and readability. Original references and license terms are recorded in the [resource review](../../../../01_Resources/00_Index/dataviz_resource_review_2026-10-23.json).

# McDonald's Ice-Cream Availability

**Marketing Analytics · By Nathan Yang**

A service team deciding which restaurants to contact needs a measure of order availability, a stable comparison population, and a forecast that uses information available before the next observation. This case uses the supplied McBroken collection for three applications:

| Module | Question | Executed Program |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M2, §2.16 | How do changing coverage, missing dates, and address keys affect an availability percentage? | `prepare.py`, `api_checks.py`, `coverage.py` |
| M6, §6.16 | How much does a policy contrast depend on the comparison country? | `policy.py` |
| M7, §7.18 | Does previous status improve forecasts on later dates, and how many origins have usable labels? | `predict.py` |

All five programs appear in full in the [lecture notes](../../06_Lecture_Notes/README.md). The parser examples are constructed edge cases; the availability calculations use the supplied observed data.

## Run the Examples

From this directory, install the dependencies in your chosen environment and run:

```sh
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python run_all.py
```

This command uses the aggregate CSV files in `data/`, runs five counterexample tests, computes the three analyses, and updates their TikZ sources. It requires no network access. The saved figure PNGs and PDF are rebuilt separately with the lecture-note builder. Python, NumPy, and pandas are sufficient; no API key is needed.

To repeat the full source assessment and reconstruct the aggregate teaching tables:

```sh
python prepare.py
python run_all.py
```

The default input is the [supplied resource bundle](../../01_Resources/02_M2_Customer_Data_and_Visualization/mcbroken_api_lab/data/). `python prepare.py --source /path/to/data` accepts another copy of that directory. The [manifest](manifest.json) records source-file sizes and SHA-256 hashes. Daily and weekly teaching tables retain the full archive commit IDs. The original resource scripts explain retrieval from the archive; their live/network collection paths were inspected but were not executed for this adaptation.

## Results and Interpretation

- The assessment reconciles 3,053,307 US store-date records with the supplied country totals. The 365-date calendar contains 356 observed US dates, nine missing US dates, and three observed dates with fewer than 2,000 records.
- There are 29,123 address keys and 13,821 exact coordinate pairs. Coordinates are a linkage diagnostic. No coordinate-based deduplication is imposed.
- The equal-day unavailable percentage is 13.18%; pooling records gives 13.37%. Alternative count thresholds are reported in [coverage_sensitivity.csv](results/coverage_sensitivity.csv).
- Around the October 28, 2024, policy effective date, a descriptive US-minus-Canada pre/post contrast is +0.65 percentage points. Using the UK gives +13.37 points. These are calculations of the contrast, with no established causal interpretation.
- In the later forecast period, previous status gives a Brier score of 0.0851 versus 0.1253 for the training-mean forecast. Usable future labels cover 72.39% of eligible origins. Results describe matched observations under the specified screens.

The [data dictionary](DATA_DICTIONARY.md) defines units and exclusions. [Results](results/README.md) describes the figures, numerical outputs, and verification evidence. These files support text-based retrieval and LLM explanations.

## Source and Rights

Underlying observations: Rashiq Zahid, [McBroken](https://mcbroken.com/). Archive: [MrFlynn/mcbroken-archive](https://github.com/MrFlynn/mcbroken-archive). The supplied extraction spans daily snapshots from October 25, 2025, through October 24, 2026, and weekly snapshots beginning in 2020. The public course files are attributed derived tables and original teaching calculations. The archive's software license is Unlicense; a separate license from McBroken for the underlying data was not established. The manifest does not assert that the data are openly licensed.

The [2024 Copyright Office final rule](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2024-10-28/pdf/2024-24563.pdf) supplies the policy effective date and scope. The calculation excludes implementation week zero and uses the same 12 pre and 12 post weeks across three countries. The case concerns evaluation design and order availability; it does not estimate a verified mechanical-failure rate or the causal effect of the exemption.

## Source: 03_Data_and_Code/McBroken/DATA_DICTIONARY.md

# McBroken Teaching Data Dictionary

The underlying field `is_broken` records the source's availability status. In the course calculations, one means **recorded order unavailability** and zero means recorded availability. A missing record has unknown status. Mechanical failure, cleaning, inventory, closure, and ordering-system problems can produce different mechanisms behind the same recorded outcome.

## Daily US Calendar

`data/daily_us.csv` has one row per UTC calendar date from October 25, 2025, through October 24, 2026.

| Variable | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| `date` | Selected snapshot's calendar date in UTC. |
| `snapshot_utc` | Time the selected archive commit was recorded, not a technician inspection or necessarily the collection time. |
| `sha` | Full archive commit identifier; the source is `https://github.com/MrFlynn/mcbroken-archive/blob/SHA/mcbroken.json`. |
| `n_checked` | Number of US records in the supplied extracted snapshot; blank if there is no US observation. |
| `n_broken` | Number of those records with `is_broken = 1`. |
| `share_unavailable` | `n_broken / n_checked`, a fraction from zero to one. |
| `offset_hours` | Commit time minus 18:00 UTC on the same date, measured in hours. |

The daily coverage program reports equal-day means and pooled record fractions. The thresholds 1,000, 2,000, and 5,000 are imposed sensitivity choices. They do not establish representativeness or identify the reason for a sparse snapshot. The nine missing US dates remain blank, including when another country was observed.

## Next-Day Transitions

`data/transitions.csv` has one row per target date and previous-status group with eligible origins. The origin is the preceding calendar date. Both origin and scored target snapshots require at least 2,000 US records and an absolute offset of no more than three hours from 18:00 UTC. Same-key matches use exact next calendar dates. They retain the original address keys; no full-year coordinate merging occurs.

| Variable | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| `date` | Target UTC calendar date. |
| `previous_unavailable` | Origin status, zero or one. |
| `n_origins` | Eligible origin records in this previous-status group, including those with missing targets. Origins after the source's final evaluation horizon are excluded. |
| `n_labeled` | Origins matched to the same key in a usable next-day target snapshot. |
| `n_unavailable` | Matched targets with unavailability status one. |

`n_unavailable <= n_labeled <= n_origins`. A zero unavailable count with zero labels does not imply availability. `n_unavailable / n_labeled` is undefined in that case. Forecast scoring weights by `n_labeled` and ignores the unavailable target status of unmatched origins while reporting their count. The model is estimated on target dates before August 1, 2026; later target dates form the test set. Full-year `n_days` and `last_seen` are excluded from features.

## Policy Window

`data/policy_window.csv` retains the selected weekly snapshots for USA, Canada (`CA`), and UK in event weeks -12 through +12 around October 28, 2024. It includes source commit timestamps, UTC dates, ISO week labels, short `commit` and full `sha`, country, counts, exact `share_unavailable`, and `event_week`. Values are fractions before the program converts them to percentages. Week zero is visible in the figure and excluded from pre/post means. The mean weights each common week equally, after requiring at least 2,000 records for USA and 500 for each comparison country.

## Assessment and Provenance

`data/assessment.json` records source row counts, duplicate and unmatched-key checks, reconciliation results, coverage, address/coordinate diagnostics, gap counts, and the scope of the status assessment. `manifest.json` identifies the six supplied source files by SHA-256 and byte size. The imported snapshot manifest contains selected commits even when their source extraction yields no usable US rows; this is why a manifest count and a panel date count can differ.

The original extractor uses Boolean conversion and a permissive number parser. The course's `api_checks.py` demonstrates stricter handling on constructed inputs. Two pinned raw snapshots were independently checked for nonboolean/missing US statuses and for agreement with supplied US totals. This spot check does not validate every historical JSON field or the underlying order-attempt mechanism.

# Agent Guide for McBroken Examples

Read the root agent guide, this folder's README, and DATA_DICTIONARY.md. Start with the managerial question and the observation process.

- Use **recorded order unavailability** for the course outcome. The `is_broken` field is not verified repair-log evidence.
- Read the aggregate tables and results before the three-million-row source panel. Use the source hashes and commit IDs for provenance.
- Distinguish a missing US date, a sparse snapshot, a missing same-key target, and an observed available record.
- Original address keys can change spelling. Exact coordinate counts diagnose possible aliases; they are not verified counts of physical restaurants. Do not merge keys automatically on coordinates.
- Match next calendar dates explicitly. Preserve the eligible-origin denominator and report usable-label coverage with forecast scores.
- Fit only on earlier target dates. Full-year `n_days`, `last_seen`, and future snapshot coverage are not origin-time predictors.
- The policy program computes descriptive country contrasts. Do not call its differences a causal policy effect or invent significance tests based on independent stores.
- The five source programs match the full Python blocks in M2 §2.16, M6 §6.16, and M7 §7.18. Update both when editing and run `scripts/check_lecture_code.py` from the repository root.
- `run_all.py` uses local teaching tables and requires no network. The original collection notebook and network retrieval scripts have separate provenance and were not rerun for this adaptation. Do not activate their scheduling template unless requested.

## Figure Descriptions

- **M02_mcbroken_coverage:** Two vertically aligned time-series panels share the same calendar. The upper panel reports observed US record counts and a dashed 2,000-record threshold; the lower panel reports the observed unavailable percentage from 0 to 100. Missing dates remain gaps. Counts change substantially while the percentage describes a changing observed population.
- **M06_mcbroken_policy:** Weekly unavailable percentages for USA, Canada, and UK share a 0–100 scale. A large UK pre-policy spike changes the comparative before/after calculation. The vertical line is the US policy effective week. The displayed comparison is descriptive.
- **M07_mcbroken_prediction:** Paired bars compare training probabilities with later observed rates within two previous-status groups. A previously unavailable record has a much higher later rate. Both later rates exceed the corresponding training forecast, indicating calibration drift in this test period.

Each figure uses the Illinois palette with redundant labels or line styles. TikZ sources and PNG companions are in `06_Lecture_Notes/figures/`; the full source programs are embedded in the Markdown and PDF notes.

Five counterexample tests verify missing-field handling, duplicate/unmatched keys, exact calendar matching, grouped versus individual Brier scores, and exclusion of later labels from training. The lecture-code checker verifies exact agreement between all embedded code and source files.

The first and last daily archive snapshots were independently retrieved by full commit ID and reconciled with the supplied national counts. Their US status fields were Boolean and nonmissing. The full historical network collection was not rerun. The supplied upstream notebook's saved outputs are reference material, not evidence that its collection code was executed during this verification.

## Source: 03_Data_and_Code/GenAI_Demand/README.md

# Demand for Generative-AI Subscriptions

Marketing Analytics. By Nathan Yang.

Three offline cases connect public signals, retention, and price sensitivity using the supplied [resource bundle](../../01_Resources/08_M8_Current_Topics_in_Marketing/genai_demand_lab/README.md). The public captures are dated observations, while the consumer panel is synthetic and generates comparisons under its stated assumptions. Its regression slopes therefore describe the simulation rather than estimates of the real AI market. The original resource files remain intact.

## Cases and Commands

From the repository root, use Python with NumPy and pandas installed. Versions tested are recorded in [results/verification.json](results/verification.json); supported ranges are in [requirements.txt](requirements.txt).

```sh
python3 03_Data_and_Code/GenAI_Demand/run_all.py
```

The command runs the three programs and eight small counterexample tests, checks that source files are unchanged, and writes aggregate CSV/JSON files plus a source-hash manifest. It makes no network requests, needs no API key, and incurs no model usage charges. The complete analysis scripts also appear in the Markdown and PDF lecture notes.

| Notes | Program | Question and Expected Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M2 §2.17 | [measurement.py](measurement.py) | Do title changes alter an apparent attention decline? June–September older-title change: -85.06%; two-title change: -16.66%, with 122 complete days. |
| M4 §4.14 | [retention.py](retention.py) | Do customers leave a provider or the paid category? Fixed-cohort partitions, endpoint versus continuous retention, and four acquisition-event types. |
| M8 §8.13 | [demand.py](demand.py) | When does a log-odds regression recover a utility price parameter? Stock slope -0.03004; flow slope -0.04987; exact binary benchmark -0.06000. |

Each program can also run independently with `python3 03_Data_and_Code/GenAI_Demand/<program>.py`. Paths resolve from the script, so a different working directory also works. Keep the resource bundle in the repository's existing location. The [data dictionary](DATA_DICTIONARY.md) defines inputs and outputs; the [result guide](results/README.md) describes their denominators.

## Interpretation

The Wikipedia calculation counts recorded events for two selected titles, without claiming unique viewers or a complete brand-attention measure. Missing title-days stay unknown. A current redirect target does not establish the full rename history; the two-title mapping comes from the supplied capture and is not a complete page-history reconstruction.

The synthetic roster contains 60,000 consumers and 40 months. Absent subscription rows mean no paid subscription within that complete simulation. Starting cohorts consist of existing January 2025 subscribers, with potentially overlapping provider memberships. Endpoint retention includes customers who left and returned. The category comparison uses exactly the same starting consumers as its provider comparison.

The simulator has heterogeneous tastes, inertia, multiple holdings, and monthly recalibration of category attractiveness. Its generated shares do not satisfy a homogeneous static binary-logit equation. Stock and flow regressions are descriptive projections. Only the separately constructed exact binary benchmark recovers its imposed parameter by construction. No causal price estimate, nested-logit parameter, or counterfactual market share is released.

## Sources and Provenance

- Egan, Mark L., Dominic Russel, Claire Shi, and Vincent Yao (2026), [Competition in Generative AI: Evidence from Consumer Demand](https://www.nber.org/papers/w35953), NBER Working Paper 35953. The abstract and bibliographic record were checked; the full paper was unavailable during this review. Detailed structural-model claims from the supplied notebook are not treated as verified paper findings.
- Fradkin, Andrey (2025), [Demand for LLMs: Descriptive Evidence on Substitution, Market Expansion, and Multihoming](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.15440). The abstract describes application-level use through OpenRouter.
- Wikimedia, [Page Views](https://doc.wikimedia.org/generated-data-platform/aqs/analytics-api/concepts/page-views.html), for the measurement definition and redirect treatment.

The source bundle, including its collectors, saved notebook, simulator, and public captures, was inspected. Those original programs were not rerun. The course analyses and tests were executed locally against the saved inputs. [manifest.json](manifest.json) records source hashes and rights; [the adaptation review](../../01_Resources/08_M8_Current_Topics_in_Marketing/genai_demand_lab/COURSE_ADAPTATION.md) records corrections and deferred extensions. Public availability alone does not establish a blanket redistribution license.

# Generative-AI Demand Data Dictionary

Inputs remain in `01_Resources/08_M8_Current_Topics_in_Marketing/genai_demand_lab/data/`. Paths below are relative to that folder. [The manifest](manifest.json) hashes the full supplied bundle. All subscription and price-simulation tables are synthetic; names resembling real providers do not make their histories empirical observations.

## Inputs Used by the Course Programs

| File | Unit and Fields | Coverage and Missingness |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wikipedia_pageviews_daily_2026-10-26.csv` | Article-date. `provider` maps the selected title; `views` counts view events. Collector specification: English Wikipedia, all access, user agent category. | 5,248 supplied title-days across five titles. Dates with no row are unknown unless the retrieval process establishes zero. The executed case uses two Claude titles, June 1–September 30, 2026, with all 244 required title-days present. |
| `synthetic_consumers.csv` | One row per `consumer_id`; `age_group`, `income_group` are simulated categories. | 60,000 consumers, including never-payers. IDs are unique. No names or actual customer records. |
| `synthetic_subscriptions.csv.gz` | Consumer-month-provider holding. `plan`, `tier`, `price` in USD/month, Boolean `promo`, Boolean `new`. | 34,186 rows. Months with no held plan have no row. Under the complete simulator's recording rule, absent holdings are zero. `new` means absent from that provider in the preceding month, including returns. |
| `synthetic_basic_prices.csv` | Available provider-month. `basic_price` is USD/month; `promo` identifies an imposed promotional price. | 179 provider-months. Missing combinations outside this table mean unavailable offers. Zero subscribers within available combinations remain possible. |
| `synthetic_dgp.json` | Parameters and calendar: `n_consumers`, `alpha_price`, `gamma_inertia`, `kappa_satiation`, and `g_trend`. | Forty months, January 2023–April 2026. Positive `alpha_price=0.06` is subtracted in utility. `g_trend` is chosen monthly to approach a target adoption path; its stored values are rounded. |

The supplied product and release tables describe imposed scenarios. Provider start months, premium selection, and quality increments are inputs to that simulation. Current prices, public launch dates, and purchase histories need separate empirical sources.

## Outputs

| File in `results/` | Unit | Definitions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wikipedia_title_days.csv` | Calendar day in the chosen 122-day window | One column per selected title; `observed_titles` counts available title counts; `selected_title_views` is their sum only when both are observed. |
| `wikipedia_months.csv` | Calendar month | `calendar_days`, `complete_days`, each title's total, combined total. A total is unknown if any required day is missing. |
| `adoption.csv` | Simulated calendar month | Population, unique payers, subscriptions, multihomers, basic subscriptions, adoption, multihoming conditional on payment, basic share among subscriptions. Conditional shares are missing when their denominator is zero. |
| `cohorts.csv` | Starting provider and months since January 2025 | Fixed `cohort_size`; mutually exclusive `same_provider`, `other_provider_only`, `no_paid_provider`; `continuous_same_provider` requires holding the original provider at every observed monthly date. |
| `acquisition_types.csv` | Acquisition-event category in April 2026 | Counts of first paid entry, category return, complete provider switch, and provider addition. One event per newly held provider; multiple events can belong to one consumer. A complete switch drops every provider held in the prior month. |
| `provider_months.csv` | Available synthetic provider-month | Basic price, promo, basic holders, new basic holders, each count divided by the full roster. Premium holdings are excluded from these two counts. |
| `price_projections.csv` | Outcome specification | Slope of log odds on price after provider/month controls; rows used; sum of squared prices after removing controls. No standard errors or causal interpretation are attached. |

JSON companions record summary counts, interpretations, and verification. `results/verification.json` records the executed environment. Each chart can be reconstructed from the CSVs without accessing an external service.

## Source: 03_Data_and_Code/GenAI_Demand/AGENTS.md

# Agent Guide for Generative-AI Demand

Read the root `AGENTS.md`, this folder's README, and the data dictionary before analysis. Use Marketing Analytics as the course title.

- Distinguish the supplied public captures from the entirely synthetic consumer panel. Treat provider names and simulated release dates as labels and inputs, not actual market observations.
- Run the offline programs for the course results. Do not silently replace captures with live values or call paid model APIs. Original collector and notebook outputs have a separate verification status.
- Preserve the full consumer denominator, available-provider support, calendar completeness, and one-row-per-observation keys. Unknown pageview records remain unknown.
- Compare provider and category retention within the same starting cohort. Report endpoint and continuous retention separately. Cohorts of existing subscribers differ from acquisition cohorts.
- `new` means newly held relative to the preceding month. Use history to separate first entry, category return, replacement of prior providers, and additions. State whether the denominator is events or consumers.
- Stock and flow price slopes are descriptive projections of a heterogeneous dynamic simulation. An exact binary-logit benchmark passes a parameter-recovery check by construction; this does not establish identification in the dynamic panel or the real market.
- Do not infer nested-logit parameters from retention gaps, public release dates from marketplace timestamps, or paid adoption from app ranks or pageviews.
- Keep matching Python blocks in M2 §2.17, M4 §4.14, and M8 §8.13 synchronized. Re-run affected analyses and counterexamples, regenerate figures when needed, and update the source-hash record without editing original data.

## Source: 03_Data_and_Code/GenAI_Demand/results/README.md

# Generative-AI Demand Results

All files are generated by the three offline course programs. Public pageviews are analyzed as a supplied dated capture; all subscription results are synthetic. See the [data dictionary](../DATA_DICTIONARY.md) for units and output fields.

- **Public signals:** 122 complete days for two selected Claude titles. June–September change is -85.06% for the older title and -16.66% for their sum. These are pageview events, not unique users, payments, or an exhaustive brand-attention measure.
- **Adoption:** 1,741 of 60,000 simulated consumers hold 1,813 subscriptions in April 2026. There are 71 multihomers, giving 4.078% conditional multihoming. The aggregate adoption path is targeted by the generator.
- **Fixed-cohort retention:** Among 430 January 2025 OpenAI subscribers, 162 hold OpenAI in January 2026, 90 hold other providers only, and 178 hold no paid provider. Only 129 hold OpenAI throughout all intervening months. These counts use the same original cohort.
- **Acquisition:** The last month has 401 newly held provider events from 400 consumers: 197 first entries, 157 returns to the category, 32 complete provider switches, and 15 provider additions.
- **Price projections:** The same 179 provider-months yield stock and flow log-odds slopes of -0.03004 and -0.04987 per dollar. Exact binary-model probabilities on the same price design recover -0.06000. The dynamic-panel slopes have a descriptive interpretation; no confidence interval or causal estimate is reported.

`verification.json` records the runtime, eight counterexample tests, and independent numerical checks. `../manifest.json` records source hashes. The original network collectors, notebook, and complete panel simulation were inspected but not executed in this course adaptation. Static tables and figures can be regenerated using the commands in the [README](../README.md).

**Python and Evidence:** Reproduce experiment calculations and specify purchase, return, and cancellation outcomes. Compare customer-row and store-mean tests under a known zero effect. Calculate prompt effects on additive and proportional-failure scales.

**Application:** Compare fixed and adaptive research designs, treatment effects, AI-generated proposals, and customer outcomes. Interpret the information-by-feedback interaction at a fixed model version. Store assignment, shared shocks, false positives, and Monte Carlo uncertainty. A workflow comparison changes the opportunity to execute, revise, and verify. Statistical detection versus profit, table-based power, and unsupported mechanism interpretations. Inverse power (Andrews, 1989) and nuisance-parameter sensitivity. Compare observationally equivalent price models and specify the randomized cells that distinguish them.

**Ethics and Regulation:** Defensible treatment designs and informed customer choice; meaningful harms left unresolved by a weak test.

# Marketing Analytics Teaching Plan

By Nathan Yang

## Meeting Structure

The Spring 2027 course meets Wednesdays, 15:30-18:20, in Wohlers Hall, Room 243, from January 20 through May 5. Excluding March 17 for spring break gives 15 meetings of 170 minutes. The [syllabus](Marketing_Analytics_Syllabus.md) records the confirmed course details. Use 13 meetings for instruction and applied work and retain two provisional presentation meetings. There are no guest speakers. The [session plan](../05_Slides/SESSION_PLAN.md) allocates the time and links all 15 slide decks.

The calendar dates are verified against the official university calendar and course listing. Graded presentation requirements, assessment weights, deadlines, attendance and late-work rules, and course-wide AI rules remain to be set. The current syllabus and schedule are linked in [course.json](../course.json).

## Learning Objectives

Students should be able to define a marketing decision and the evidence needed to inform it; construct and assess a customer dataset; interpret descriptive, predictive, and causal results; evaluate product, targeting, and retention decisions; and reproduce an analysis with Python. AI-assisted coding is integrated into the specification, implementation, verification, and interpretation of each analysis.

Students should also be able to distinguish firm outcomes from customer value, identify consequences omitted by a commercial objective, and assess which public legal source applies to a proposed action. A defensible recommendation states the population, estimand, assumptions, uncertainty, customer consequences, and relevant regulatory scope.

## Topic Sequence

| Meetings | Module | Topics |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | M1 | Marketing questions, Python, data contracts, and AI-assisted coding |
| 2–3 | M2 | Customer measurement, cleaning, nutrition-informed restrictions, visualization, and coverage |
| 4 | M3 | Regression, interactions, interpretation, uncertainty, and claim support |
| 5–6 | M4 | Conjoint, product design, concept screening, segmentation, lifetime value, and customer choice |
| 7 | M5 | Text, sentiment, social media, networks, and review provenance |
| 8 | M1–M5 | Provisional project-evidence and presentation meeting |
| 9–10 | M6 | Experiments, causal comparisons, policy evaluation, and customer outcomes |
| 11–12 | M7 | Prediction, validation, targeting, recommendation, and access |
| 13–14 | M8, M9 | Adaptive systems, marketing budgets, generative AI, Marketing Dialectics, retention, and regulation |
| 15 | M1–M8 | Provisional integrated-decision and presentation meeting |

## Cases and Applied Work

Use mHealth throughout the eight modules. Synthetic examples provide small calculations that can be checked by hand. Each data application links complete Python, input definitions, sample restrictions, and expected output.

Ethics and regulation recur within the methods. The [module integration guide](../06_Lecture_Notes/ETHICS_AND_REGULATION.md) connects privacy, customer representation, claim substantiation, pricing, retention, review authenticity, experimentation, and delivery. Session 14 reserves 75 minutes for Marketing Dialectics, customer outcomes, and regulatory scope. The chapter applies Kantian critique, scrutiny of conflicting interests (Hume, 1741; Smith, 1776), and Confucian accounts of conduct to marketing practices. The final 15 minutes compare reasoned recommendations; no extra meeting is added. Presentation discussions include customer consequences and the strength of the evidence supporting the recommendation.

The [lecture notes](../06_Lecture_Notes/README.md) provide detailed explanations and runnable programs. # Ethics and Regulation in Marketing Analytics

Marketing decisions affect customers' information, access, time, money, and ability to choose. A commercial metric captures only some of these consequences. Evaluate the action, the customer outcome, and the relevant legal obligation separately, then explain how each affects the decision.

## A Retention-Procedure Case

A firm compares direct renewal with optional interactions before the same final offer. In the synthetic example, renewal probabilities are 0.10, 0.20, and 0.60. Firm margin is 11 dollars per renewal, and the customer loses 10 dollars from a renewal under the imposed preference ordering. Relative to direct choice at 0.20, selecting the 0.60 procedure increases expected firm profit by 4.40 dollars and lowers expected customer value by 4 dollars per eligible customer. Combined surplus rises by 0.40 dollars. The aggregate gain therefore coexists with a distributional loss.

These conclusions require the stated stakes and stable probabilities. A measured renewal increase alone does not identify customer value. Evaluate informed willingness to continue, cancellation completion, elapsed time, subsequent charges, and the ability to refuse optional interaction. The [complete calculation](../03_Data_and_Code/Lecture_Examples/retention_welfare.py), [aggregate table](../03_Data_and_Code/Lecture_Examples/retention_welfare.csv), and [TikZ figure](figures/M08_retention_welfare.tex) reproduce the imposed comparison.

## Discussion and Applied Work

For a proposed marketing action, identify the customer population, the information available, and the commercial objective. Describe the customer's feasible choices and the consequences outside that objective. Select a benchmark, a customer outcome, and a measurement horizon. Then identify the jurisdiction, covered conduct, effective date, and authority of the relevant primary source. A proposed assessment or discussion exercise does not establish an assignment requirement or grade weight.

# Earnings Calls: Pricing Communication

A retail communications team must decide which public pricing statements deserve closer reading before recommending a message or policy. The supplied conference-call collection supports measuring disclosure, comparing speaker exposure, and assessing the evidence behind a pricing claim. A dictionary hit is evidence of specified language. Adoption, consumer harm, and legal violations require additional evidence.

## Files and Reproduction

The [manifest](manifest.json) records original and exported SHA-256 hashes. `data/` contains 2,326 call records, 971 dictionary-match records, a 123-firm roster, 19 dictionary terms, and seven purposeful interpretation cases. Source call dates run from November 2, 2021 through November 2, 2026. The sample includes current-index constituents and selected comparison firms; it is not a probability sample of businesses or a historical market census.

Use Python with pandas and NumPy. Verified with Python 3.13, pandas 2.2.3, and NumPy 2.1.3. From this folder:

```sh
python assessment.py
python disclosure.py
python construct_checks.py
python event_windows.py
python test_examples.py
python build_figures.py
```

The first four commands write reproducible CSV/JSON outputs into `results/`. Nine counterexample tests check missingness, denominators, role exposure, event boundaries, firm weights, dictionary meaning, and the text-free export. `build_figures.py` reads those outputs and writes three editable TikZ figures into the lecture notes. It requires the course repository layout.

The optional `python prepare.py --source /path/to/pricing_risk_earnings_calls` reconstructs the teaching inputs from the instructor's original local bundle. Students can run every analysis using the committed `data/` files without that bundle, a network connection, an API key, or transcript scraping. No dependencies are installed by the scripts.

## Worked Cases

| Notes and Session | Decision and Comparison | Program |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M2 §2.19; S02 | Retain firms with no matches; distinguish missing text from a negative call; compare full and selected denominators | `assessment.py` |
| M5 §5.14; S07 | Compare call incidence and role-specific word exposure; assess retrieval versus substantive interpretation | `disclosure.py`, `construct_checks.py` |
| M6 §6.18; S10 | Compare 60-, 90-, and 120-day windows around a public clarification, with common firms and alternative weights | `event_windows.py` |
| M8 §8.16; S14 | Separate pricing infrastructure, intentions, implementation, consumer consequences, and regulatory evidence | `data/interpretation_cases.csv`; M5 code and outputs |

The notes include the complete four analysis programs. The [results guide](results/README.md) states the numerical findings and their scope. The [data dictionary](DATA_DICTIONARY.md) defines keys, flags, units, and observation levels. [LLM exercises](LLM_EXERCISES.md) provide specifications and adversarial checks for AI-assisted coding and annotation.

## Source: 03_Data_and_Code/Earnings_Calls/DATA_DICTIONARY.md

# Earnings-Call Data Dictionary

## Observation Levels

`firms.csv` has one row per ticker in the supplied 123-firm roster. `calls.csv` has one row per unique `call_id`. `mentions.csv` has one row per regex occurrence, keyed by `mention_id`; several occurrences can belong to the same call, turn, or sentence. Joining calls directly to mentions repeats call-level quantities. Aggregate matches to call first, then use a validated one-to-one join when constructing call-level rates.

## Inputs

| File | Fields and Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `firms.csv` | `ticker`, company, supplied sector group; `inclusion` describes selection; `n_calls_in_window` includes empty-text records; provider list URL |
| `calls.csv` | Stable call ID, ticker, company, supplied group, call date, fiscal year/quarter, source URL; `n_turns`; `qa_start_turn` is a heuristic index, with -1 meaning undetected; total and role word counts; core, broad, and per-term regex counts |
| `mentions.csv` | Match ID, call ID, ticker/date; dictionary term/category/tier; heuristic role and section; turn index. No transcript text or speaker names |
| `dictionary.csv` | Term ID, category, core/broad tier, Python regex, case-sensitive flag (0/1). Tier describes retrieval specificity, not a verified business practice |
| `interpretation_cases.csv` | Seven selected source match IDs and URLs, original term IDs, course-authored paraphrases, evidence scope, and interpretation. Purposeful examples, not representative accuracy labels |

Fiscal quarters can differ from calendar quarters. The time-series output derives calendar quarters from `call_date`. The first and last calendar quarters have partial date support. Interior calendar coverage alone does not establish complete source capture.

## Derived Flags and Rates

`text_observed` means `words_total > 0`. The empty `DLTR_FY2026Q2` record remains in the coverage assessment, with unknown `has_core`. `has_core` is 1 if at least one core match occurs in an observed call and 0 otherwise; NaN denotes unobserved text. This binary indicator measures dictionary occurrence, not confirmed adoption. `qa_detected` means `qa_start_turn >= 0`; it is a parsing flag, not evidence that no Q&A occurred when false.

`core_call_rate` divides positive calls by observed calls. `per_10000_words` divides role-specific core matches by words attributed to that role in the same call sample and multiplies by 10,000. Management words include prepared remarks and Q&A; analyst words are attributed to Q&A. Unknown/operator words can appear in total words without entering either role denominator.

`firm_coverage.csv` retains Winmark (WINA), with zero supplied calls and an unknown rate. Firms with observed calls and no matches have rate zero. `event_windows.csv` uses calendar-day distance from February 27, 2024, excludes the event day, and includes the endpoints at ±60, ±90, or ±120 days. `firms_in_both_windows` retains firms with at least one observed call in each window. `share_percent` weights calls equally; `firm_equal_share_percent` averages within-firm rates equally.

## Interpretation Conditions

Disclosure is selected by the firm, analysts, transcript coverage, and the vocabulary. Roles and Q&A sections are heuristic. The source retains only truncated excerpts, so applying the dictionary to an excerpt cannot reconstruct whole-call recall. No direct prices, customer outcomes, policy-adoption labels, or independently validated legal outcomes are present. Repeated calls within firms also share business and communication conditions; a statistical generalization would require a defensible sampling target and dependence-aware uncertainty calculation.

## Source: 03_Data_and_Code/Earnings_Calls/LLM_EXERCISES.md

# AI-Assisted Coding and Interpretation

## Preserve the Population

Give an assistant the data dictionary and five rows from each metadata table. Request a call-level summary that retains all firms and distinguishes unknown text from observed zero matches. Require explicit keys, join cardinalities, denominator definitions, and a check against hand calculations. Run `assessment.py` and compare 112/2,325 with 112/445. Ask the assistant to explain which population each rate describes before accepting its code.

## Match Numerators to Exposure

Request raw role counts and core occurrences per 10,000 role words, first for all observed calls and then for calls with detected Q&A. Ask it to predict how unequal speaking time might change the comparison. Run `disclosure.py`. Introduce a missing-Q&A call with many management words and verify that excluding the call removes both its words and its matches. The fixture in `test_examples.py` provides a hand-checkable counterexample.

## Distinguish Language from a Business Practice

Use `data/interpretation_cases.csv` and the synthetic sentences in `construct_checks.py` locally. Request fields `case_id`, `priced_object`, `timing`, `speaker_claim`, `evidence_scope`, and `needs_more_context`. Require unknown values when evidence is insufficient. Compare responses with the recorded interpretations, especially the planned-test, price-display, and shelf-infrastructure cases. These exercises specify a workflow; no model responses or measured LLM performance are supplied.

For a future empirical evaluation, define the construct before annotation, draw a probability sample that includes retrieved and nonretrieved passages, record sampling probabilities, and obtain independent labels with adjudication. Hold out firms or later calls to limit repeated-language leakage. Freeze the dictionary or prompt before evaluating that holdout. Weighted precision and recall require the target population and sufficient verified labels. An evaluation of hits alone cannot estimate recall. Use approved local text or appropriately authorized sources for any annotation task.

## Challenge a Causal Explanation

Ask for before/after rates around February 27, 2024, with exact window endpoints, an excluded event day, all available firms, and firms observed in both windows. Run `event_windows.py`. Have the assistant reconcile why five versus two mentions can coexist with an unchanged 2/27 call rate. Require a separate statement of the treatment, outcome, and counterfactual that would be needed to identify a causal effect on disclosure, prices, or customer outcomes.

# Earnings-Call Results

Executed November 2, 2026 using the supplied snapshot. Four analysis programs and nine counterexample tests passed. The source hash manifest verifies the exported inputs; no live transcript collection or model API was run.

- The roster has 123 firms; 122 have supplied calls. Of 2,326 calls, 2,325 have positive word counts. The empty Dollar Tree record is unknown for language presence.
- Core terms occur in 112 observed calls (4.8172%). Restricting the denominator to 445 calls with any dictionary match raises the apparent rate to 25.1685% by selection.
- Core-call rates are 36/1,241 (2.9009%) in retail, 9/445 (2.0225%) in restaurants, and 67/639 (10.4851%) in the supplied comparison group. These are call-weighted disclosure rates in a selected corpus.
- Management accounts for 127 core matches in 16,685,338 attributed words (0.076115 per 10,000 words); analysts account for 23 in 2,761,999 words (0.083273). Among 2,240 nonempty calls with detected Q&A, the management rate is 115/15,985,597 × 10,000 = 0.071940; the analyst rate remains 0.083273. Role and format differences remain material.
- In the common-firm comparison group around the February 27, 2024 clarification, 27 calls from the same 27 firms appear in each 90-day window. Core occurrences fall from five to two; two calls contain core language in each window, so incidence remains 7.4074%. This descriptive comparison supplies no untreated counterfactual.
- Eight synthetic sentences expose lexical and substantive differences: denial, future intention, questions, price displays, and infrastructure can match; a paraphrase of current demand-responsive fares can fail to match. Seven selected real-call paraphrases provide interpretation cases. No population accuracy estimate follows.

`call_status.csv`, `firm_coverage.csv`, and `assessment.json` document inclusion. `group_rates.csv`, `role_rates.csv`, and `quarter_rates.csv` document denominators. `event_windows.csv` records both samples, all three windows, call counts, and firm-equal rates. `synthetic_construct_checks.csv` and `interpretation_summary.csv` separate imposed tests from actual disclosure examples. The three TikZ figures are generated from these tables with explicit value checks.

# Marketing Analytics

**BADM 534 | Spring 2027 | Section A | CRN 77732**

| Course Information | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Instructor | Nathan Yang |
| Email | [ncyang@illinois.edu](mailto:ncyang@illinois.edu) |
| Office Hours | By appointment |
| Class Meetings | Wednesdays, 15:30-18:20 (3:30-6:20 p.m.) |
| Location | Wohlers Hall, Room 243 |
| Meeting Dates | January 20-May 5, 2027; no class March 17 |

## Course Description

Marketing decisions require evidence about customer preferences, behavior, and responses to a firm's actions. The course applies measurement, visualization, regression, conjoint analysis, segmentation, lifetime value, text and network analysis, experiments, causal inference, prediction, and recommendation to product design, acquisition, retention, pricing, and budgets.

Students use AI-assisted Python to specify questions, verify calculations, and interpret results. Marketing Dialectics applies Kantian, Confucian, and Scanlonian philosophy to agency, conflicts of interest, and regulation. Disciplinary history and the phenomena–noumena distinction (Kant, 1781/1787) connect measurement to persons and obligations. Chicago price theory supplies cases on willingness to pay, rational addiction, compensation, and market justification. Students assess objectives, evidentiary standards, false alarms, and missed harm, applying the same standards to claims and criticisms.

## Learning Objectives

- Define a managerial decision, the relevant population, and the evidence needed to inform it.
- Evaluate which ends deserve pursuit, who has authority to select them, and what obligations the decision creates, distinguishing empirical knowledge from practical justification.
- Assess how data are produced and accessed; define observation units, denominators, missing values, and reproducible transformations.
- Apply marketing analytics methods; distinguish descriptive patterns, prediction, and causal effects; justify controls, populations, and observation windows.
- Evaluate AI-assisted workflows through independent checks, statistical design, meaningful-effect bounds, and the costs of false positives and missed harm.
- Justify recommendations using evidence, clear figures, customer consequences, and critical examination of ethical premises.
- Reconstruct arguments; distinguish fit, identification, and valuation; justify investigation or protection under uncertainty; state reasons for revising a conclusion.

## Class Format and Materials

Meetings combine instructor-led explanations, worked examples, Python, and discussion. Students predict results, inspect equations and code, and defend or revise conclusions. The 15 meetings last 170 minutes each and include two project discussion and presentation sessions; presentation requirements will be specified separately.

The [course repository](https://github.com/nene88991999/BADM534-Marketing-Analytics) provides [lecture notes](../06_Lecture_Notes/README.md), [session slides](../05_Slides/README.md), and [data with runnable Python](../03_Data_and_Code/README.md). Markdown companions support search and LLM use. Resource recommendations provide background; assigned readings will be identified separately.

# AI Workflow Evaluation and Economics

Three original synthetic examples connect AI-assisted coding to experimental design, prediction, and economic decisions. They use Python 3.10 or later and the standard library. All inputs are constructed for the course on November 4, 2026. No customer records, downloaded programs, provider credentials, or model API calls enter these calculations.

## Run the Examples

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 03_Data_and_Code/AI_Workflows/factorial.py
python3 03_Data_and_Code/AI_Workflows/repeated_selection.py
python3 03_Data_and_Code/AI_Workflows/investment.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s 03_Data_and_Code/AI_Workflows -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

Paths resolve relative to each script, so commands also work from another directory. Each program overwrites its own derived files in `results/`. Repeated selection uses a fixed seed and two separate pseudorandom streams. The inputs are embedded in the scripts; change them there before regenerating outputs and reconciling the notes and figures. All programs and five independent small-case checks were executed successfully.

## Inputs, Outputs, and Interpretation

| Program and Notes | Output | Observation Unit and Units | Expected Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [factorial.py](factorial.py); M6 §6.19 | [Four conditions](results/factorial_cells.csv), [contrasts](results/factorial_results.json) | Model-by-library condition; 100 assigned tasks per cell; counts and pass fractions; JSON contrasts in percentage points | Model gain 5 points without the library and 15 with it; interaction 10 points; joint change 25 points |
| [repeated_selection.py](repeated_selection.py); M7 §7.20 | [Selection results](results/selection_results.csv), [simulation metadata](results/selection_metadata.json) | Candidate-count scenario, averaged over 2,000 independent repetitions; accuracy and Monte Carlo SE in fractions | At 100 candidates, expected selected development accuracy 0.6393 and expected fresh accuracy 0.5 |
| [investment.py](investment.py); M8 §8.17 | [Reuse costs](results/reuse_costs.csv), [price bounds](results/price_bounds.csv), [summary](results/investment_results.json) | Number of uses and hours; separately, pricing scenario and dollars per customer | Reuse breaks even at 12 uses; initial price interval 40–80 dollars; shared-adoption floor 30 exceeds ceiling 20 |

In the factorial CSV, `model=0` denotes the earlier configuration and `model=1` the newer configuration; `library=0/1` denotes absence/presence. `assigned` is the denominator and `passed` the numerator. Counts are stipulated, not experimental observations. Every cell refers to the same task population, rubric, deadline, and resource limits.

In repeated selection, each candidate is correct with probability one-half, independently across candidates and cases. Each has 80 development cases and 200 fresh cases. Within a repetition, the first 1, 5, 20, and 100 candidates form nested sets; the first candidate wins a tie. The test stream never enters selection. Monte Carlo SE describes uncertainty in a simulated mean across repetitions, not a deployment confidence interval. All inputs are public teaching material; the simulation represents fresh evaluation without creating a private assessment set.

Reuse assumes equal accepted output quality, six setup hours, two hours per existing analysis, and 1.25 execution plus 0.25 upkeep hours per reusable analysis over a hypothetical quarter. Pricing holds delivered value at 200 dollars, buyer burden at 40 dollars, fixed cost at 1,000 dollars, and conditional sales at 50. Seller unit cost and the customer's net outside-option utility vary. No demand response or equilibrium price is estimated. No missing values or exclusions are applied.

## Course Connections

- M1 §1.12 distinguishes faulty code, missing evidence, and an unclear analytical target.
- M4 §4.16 connects willingness to pay with customer effort and outside options.
- M5 §5.15 applies fresh evaluation to earnings-call prompt revision.
- M6 §6.19 and M7 §7.20 include complete runnable programs and the sampling conditions.
- M8 §§8.17–8.18 connect reusable work, competitive pricing, and selective model upgrades.
- Sessions 01, 05, 07, 09, 11, and 14 include the relevant discussion or calculation.

The [lecture notes](../../06_Lecture_Notes/README.md) contain all three programs verbatim. Four editable TikZ figures use the same aggregate values, Illinois colors, and text descriptions. The tests check additive contrasts, a binomial maximum against exhaustive binary enumeration, the tie rule, maintenance that prevents cost recovery, and equality at the participation and cost bounds. Passing these checks verifies the specified arithmetic; the hypothetical inputs establish no provider performance or customer demand.

# Agent Guide for AI Workflow Examples

Read the root guide and this folder's README before answering questions or changing code. All examples are synthetic and use only Python's standard library. Do not present their outcomes as measured LLM accuracy, an experiment with analysts, observed labor savings, or estimated customer demand.

Keep development and test outcomes separate in the selection program. Preserve the explicit independence assumptions, nested candidate sets, tie rule, and simulation metadata. A Monte Carlo standard error concerns simulation precision. Real evaluation needs an appropriate task population, assignment unit, independent labels, and protection against repeated adaptation to the same outcomes.

Retain the conditional nature of sales volume, monetary valuations, equal output quality, and maintenance costs. Price bounds are participation and cost-recovery conditions, not a pricing equilibrium or forecast. Hours and dollars are separate units.

After changing calculations, run the affected programs and `test_examples.py`, update the full code blocks in M6, M7, or M8, reconcile figures with the aggregate CSVs, and run `scripts/check_lecture_code.py`. Follow the lecture-note and slide guides when updating those artifacts. No external model calls are needed for these examples.

# Consumer Agency and Recent Marketing Research

How should a firm evaluate an interface that raises adoption or retention while weakening customers' understanding or ability to leave? This collection connects recent marketing research to consumer agency, clustering, and cancellation policy.

## Collection and Review

The November 5, 2026 census contains **886 unique DOI records** from Journal of Marketing, Journal of Marketing Research, and Marketing Science. The date rule includes records with an online or issue-publication date from January 1, 2023 through November 5, 2026. The same paper appears once even when its online and issue years differ. Future 2026 publications are outside this snapshot.

Crossref queries using each journal's verified ISSNs establish the metadata census. Publisher tables of contents have not been exhaustively reconciled against it. Screening removes 62 front-matter, correction, retraction, or related notice records, leaving 824 eligible records, including substantive editorials and commentaries. The screen is not a claim that every eligible record is an empirical research article.

| Journal | DOI Records | Eligible | Retrieved Full Texts or Related Versions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Journal of Marketing | 276 | 273 | 48 |
| Journal of Marketing Research | 266 | 262 | 25 |
| Marketing Science | 344 | 289 | 30 |
| Total | 886 | 824 | 103 |

There are **721 eligible records without a verified retrieved full text**. Publisher restrictions and inaccessible repository links limit coverage. The UIUC Library route available in the browser still returned a publisher access screen on November 5; a separate desktop session could not be checked while the Mac was locked. No institutional entitlement is inferred from a browser login or an OpenAlex open-access flag.

The collection provides **144 original paper summaries**, covering every retrieved paper plus 41 selected abstract-only records. Most summaries are based on abstracts; selected teaching cases additionally use full-text discussion or conclusion sections. Each card states its actual evidence basis. The review does not claim a complete assessment of the methods and results in all 103 downloads.

## Rights, Versions, and Identity

Research PDFs are organized by journal in Dropbox-only `local_papers/` subfolders. Their redistribution rights have not been individually cleared, so the public repository contains metadata, original summaries, and links. Open availability alone is insufficient permission to republish a PDF. Official legal texts have separate provenance in `Policy/sources.json`.

Retrieved versions include published articles, accepted manuscripts, working papers, and one dissertation containing an earlier related chapter. The ledger identifies those differences. Numerical results in an early version must be checked against the version being cited. Downloads were checked for PDF format, extractable text, and title consistency. Two unrelated documents found through repository links were rejected; one was subsequently replaced with the correct article. The remaining rejected document is counted as an access gap.

## Interpretation of Agency

The coding distinguishes reported choice concerns, possible dual use, protective mechanisms, and concerns not established on the reviewed evidence. A possible misuse is an inference about a mechanism, not an allegation about the authors or proof that a firm deployed it. The [codebook](../../03_Data_and_Code/Consumer_Agency_Literature/CODEBOOK.md) states definitions and unresolved reliability limitations.

Clustering describes the mechanism composition of the selected review sample. Access, publication selection, abstract coverage, and coding choices affect its result. The frequency of a mechanism in papers does not measure the frequency or severity of agency erosion in markets.

## Source: 01_Resources/13_Consumer_Agency_and_Recent_Research/Policy/README.md

# Subscription Cancellation and Consumer Choice

A cancellation process determines whether a customer's decision to leave becomes an effective end to recurring charges. Retention can rise because service quality improves, because a consumer knowingly accepts a useful offer, or because the interface obstructs exit. Those mechanisms have different implications for customer welfare and for the interpretation of lifetime value.

Status checked November 5, 2026. The entries below distinguish legal instruments, jurisdictions, covered transactions, and effective dates. They are a teaching source record, not a complete statement of every applicable subscription law.

## United States Federal Rules

The Eighth Circuit vacated the FTC's 2024 Negative Option Rule on July 8, 2025 after finding a procedural failure involving the required preliminary regulatory analysis. The decision removed that rule; it did not repeal separate statutory protections. See the [court's opinion](https://ecf.ca8.uscourts.gov/opndir/25/07/243137P.pdf), especially pages 19-23, and the local [PDF](Eighth_Circuit_2025_Vacatur.pdf).

Effective February 12, 2026, the FTC recodified the earlier prenotification rule to conform to the court's decision. That older rule has a narrower scope centered on prenotification plans for merchandise. The FTC then issued an advance notice of proposed rulemaking on March 13, 2026 seeking input on negative-option practices. That notice does not itself establish a replacement cancellation obligation. The October 14, 2026 information-collection notice also concerns the restored earlier rule. Sources: [February final action](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-02-12/pdf/2026-02866.pdf), [March notice](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-03-13/pdf/2026-04952.pdf), and [October notice](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-14/pdf/2026-20971.pdf). Local copies: [February](FTC_2026_Recodification.pdf), [March](FTC_2026_Proposed_Rulemaking.pdf), and [October](FTC_2026_Information_Collection.pdf).

The Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act, enacted December 29, 2010, separately addresses online negative-option transactions. Section 4 requires clear disclosure of material terms before obtaining billing information, express informed consent before charging, and a simple mechanism to stop recurring charges. These requirements provide a federal baseline for the covered transactions. Source: [Public Law 111-345, Section 4](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PLAW-111publ345/pdf/PLAW-111publ345.pdf), codified at 15 U.S.C. §8403; [local PDF](ROSCA_2010.pdf).

## California

California strengthened its Automatic Renewal Law effective July 1, 2025. The Attorney General's September 2025 guidance describes coverage of consumer automatic-renewal and continuous-service arrangements, including free trials that become paid subscriptions. It emphasizes express consent, reminders, and straightforward cancellation. Consumers who enroll online must be able to cancel online without obstructive or delaying steps. Source: [California Attorney General's guidance](https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-bonta-issues-consumer-alert-california%E2%80%99s-automatic-renewal-law).

## New York City

New York City's rule took effect October 1, 2026. It addresses automatic-renewal and continuous-service arrangements through disclosure, consent, and cancellation requirements. Section 5-110.2 requires a simple cancellation process that is as easy as the method used to enroll, with cancellation available through enrollment media. It bars obstruction and unreasonable delay. Retention offers may be made subject to the rule's restrictions; they may not obstruct or unreasonably delay cancellation. Section 5-110.3 contains sector exclusions, including specified regulated financial, insurance, alarm, and franchise-related arrangements. Coverage must be assessed before applying the rule to a business. Sources: [official city guidance](https://www.nyc.gov/main/click-to-cancel) and [adopted rule](https://www.nyc.gov/content/dam/nycgov/nyc-main/pdf/2026/Click-to-Cancel-Rule.pdf). The official text was read online; the direct PDF transfer returned an access error.

## Measurement and Evaluation

For a cancellation flow, define the eligible population as customers who initiate a cancellation attempt. Measure successful cancellation, elapsed time, required interactions, subsequent charges, refunds, understanding of any retention offer, and later complaints. Preserve enrollment channel, jurisdiction, and contract dates. A lower cancellation rate can reflect useful voluntary retention or a failure to execute the customer's intent; the event log alone may not separate them.

An evaluation should compare lawful, transparent service or cancellation designs and track whether customers achieve their stated goals. A jurisdiction-level policy comparison also needs a treatment date, covered population, comparable controls, pre-policy trends, and attention to firm-wide interface changes that spill across jurisdictions. A rule's effective date is an intervention date, not automatic causal identification.

## File Companions

This Markdown file summarizes the substantive cancellation provisions relevant to the course. It does not reproduce procedural arguments, all exceptions, or unrelated rules sharing Federal Register pages. The PDFs retain the official text and pagination; [sources.json](sources.json) records download URLs, date, and checksums. Recheck current law before using these materials for an actual business decision or a later course offering.

# Consumer Agency in Recent Marketing Research

A subscription manager must distinguish retention created by customer value from retention created by obstructing exit. This example connects that decision to a review of recent marketing research, explicit mechanism coding, and clustering.

## Inputs and Coverage

`coded_papers.csv` contains 144 reviewed DOI records drawn from the 2023-2026 journal census. The [resource library](../../01_Resources/13_Consumer_Agency_and_Recent_Research/README.md) provides the complete census, access gaps, source links, and individual managerial summaries. `reviewed_summaries.json` preserves the original annotations; `review_evidence.json` records selected full-text checks. These are evidence-based teaching annotations, not simulated articles or independently adjudicated labels.

The primary analysis uses 48 retrieved papers with reported choice concerns or potential dual use. Sensitivity analyses use all 84 reviewed papers with those classifications, and 60 retrieved papers including protective mechanisms. Seven additional protective papers have no positive feature under the mechanism codebook and remain outside the latter comparison. Read [CODEBOOK.md](CODEBOOK.md) before interpreting any counts.

## Run the Analysis

From the repository root, with Python 3.13 and the packages in `requirements.txt` available (tested with Python 3.13.5):

```bash
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Consumer_Agency_Literature/cluster.py
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Consumer_Agency_Literature/assess_coverage.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s 03_Data_and_Code/Consumer_Agency_Literature -p 'test_*.py'
```

The analysis reads public CSV inputs and performs no network requests. Paths are relative to each script. Seed 534 controls the sensitivity calculations. The tested package versions and output counts are in [results/summary.json](results/summary.json). Main findings and their scope appear in [results/README.md](results/README.md).

Each analysis sample produces paper-level assignments, cluster sizes, cluster profiles, feature prevalence, candidate-K scores, and subsample stability draws. Feature shares may sum above one because papers can have several mechanisms; cluster shares sum to one. No causal effect is estimated from the literature counts.

## Update the Collection

`collect.py` retrieves Crossref journal metadata and OpenAlex locations. `download.py` attempts publisher and open-repository copies, records failures, checks PDF identity, and stops requesting a host after an access block. It requires `curl` and `pdftotext`; set `AGENCY_PDFTOTEXT` if the latter is not on PATH. `add_sources.py` preserves manually verified author-copy locations. These acquisition scripts contact external sources only when explicitly run.

`build_catalog.py` combines the cached acquisition records and original reviews. Its raw metadata inputs and full texts remain in the Dropbox-only `local_sources/` and `local_papers/` folders. Rebuilding that catalog therefore requires those local inputs; students can reproduce the clustering from the public CSV without them. `fetch_policy.py` retrieves official legal documents and records checksums. Access to an article does not establish permission to redistribute it.

## Interpretation

The largest primary cluster concerns social influence. This conclusion applies to the accessible, coded subset. The lower agreement under feature perturbations shows why a precise empirical claim about the dominant form of agency erosion would require more complete access and independently validated coding. Policy relevance can be high even for mechanisms with few papers: cancellation rules directly govern exit friction, while journal counts measure research attention and selection into this collection.
