## Source: 01_Resources/32_Graph_Coarsening/SOURCE_REVIEW.md

# Preserving Information When a Network is Compressed

A retailer may reduce a large network to a smaller set of zones to lower the cost of analysis. The resulting representation needs to preserve the outcomes used in the decision. Connections between groups, average features, travel times, and customer-specific predictions are distinct objects. GraCo makes several of these choices explicit and provides a useful setting for evaluating the assumptions embedded in an analytical workflow.

## Partition, Aggregation, and Reconstruction

GraCo assigns each of the original $N$ nodes to one of $n$ supernodes. The binary membership matrix $Q_b$ has shape $N\times n$, with one unit entry per row. For an undirected weighted adjacency matrix $A$, the coarse adjacency is $A_c=Q_b^\top A Q_b$. An off-diagonal entry sums the weights crossing between two groups. The default builder removes diagonal entries, so within-group edges are absent from the returned coarse adjacency. [Paper, §2; pinned builder](reference/core/builders.py).

Node features require a separate reduction matrix $P$. Under binary lifting and the default pseudoinverse, $P=(Q_b^\top Q_b)^{-1}Q_b^\top$ averages features within each group. The lifted values $Q_bPx$ assign each member its group's mean. Group sizes must accompany those means when calculating a population average or total. GraCo's default lifting is instead degree-normalized for `normalized_self_loop`; the simple averaging formula applies when the combinatorial convention is chosen. This distinction matters when interpreting a feature as spending, demand, or population. [Paper, §3; pinned normalization code](reference/core/q.py).

Preserving the feature values used to form a representation does not establish preservation of a different decision outcome. The four-zone example in [CASE_DESIGN.md](CASE_DESIGN.md) retains its revenue feature and associated quadratic graph energy exactly while losing travel inside a merged zone. The implication follows from the constructed graph. GraCo supplies no general guarantee of preserving shortest travel times, service thresholds, causal effects, or willingness to pay.

## A Metric Changes the Method Ranking

Table 4 compares methods on Cora and PubMed under a common self-loop-normalized Laplacian. Its criteria include restricted spectral approximation, eigenvalue error, convolution-matching error, and label purity. Local variation has Cora RSA 0.67 versus Leiden's 1.58, where lower is better. Leiden has lower convolution-matching error, 29.2 versus 32.9 thousand. Both report an achieved reduction ratio of 0.70 for these rows. The preferred method therefore changes with the criterion even in this selected same-ratio comparison. [Paper, Appendix B.5, p. 25](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.01200v1#A2.SS5).

The broader benchmark also requires attention to the achieved reduction. On PubMed, Table 4 reports ratios of 0.79 for METIS and 0.64 for GBGC against a requested 0.70. Those methods produce different-sized outputs. Runtime comparisons need the original graph size, retained size, hardware, preprocessing, and tuning budget. The paper distinguishes out-of-memory, timeout, and solver failures. Its numerical rankings are specific to the reported defaults and datasets.

For marketing, select the primary outcome before comparing compression methods: for example, retained access to an available store, held-out recommendation quality, recall for a small group, or profit under a specified policy. Spectral and feature metrics can help explain how the representation changed. They do not establish the marketing outcome by themselves. The paper explicitly leaves training graph neural networks on the coarsened graphs to a later release (§1, p. 2), so this release supplies no trained-model marketing validation.

## Preprocessing Changes the Population and Relationships

The pinned [preprocessing function](reference/loaders/preprocess.py) defaults to removing self-loops, symmetrizing the graph, and retaining only its largest connected component. For weighted reciprocal edges, symmetrization uses their mean. These transformations support the mathematical assumptions of the implemented methods. For marketing data, they can also change the measured population or the meaning of a relation.

The existing synthetic retail network has 800 people, including 150 at a disconnected origin. Keeping only the largest connected component removes that origin. Known five-minute access remains 550 people, while its reported share changes from $550/800=68.75\%$ to $550/650=84.62\%$. The increase of 15.87 percentage points comes entirely from changing the denominator. The origin also has a store with unknown status; retaining it preserves the original lower and upper access bounds. [Existing case, M5 §5.21](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md).

Direction can carry substantive information in referrals, follows, transfers, and one-way travel. Averaging reciprocal weights creates a new relation. A student should state the edge meaning and target population before accepting this default. Turning off a transformation also requires checking that the selected algorithm supports the resulting graph. Component-wise analysis or preserving excluded nodes in a separate accounting table may be appropriate for the decision.

## Label Purity and Held-Out Prediction

The [pinned `max_acc` implementation](reference/metrics/structural.py) first finds the majority label of each group using all node labels. Its `all` output is the best possible accuracy of a classifier constrained to predict one constant label per group on those same nodes. This is an oracle diagnostic of information lost by the partition. It is not accuracy from training a classifier and evaluating new outcomes.

The implementation then evaluates that same all-node majority on each supplied mask. It does not recompute a separate optimal constant within each mask. Consequently, `test` and `masked` are scores of the global-majority assignment and need not be upper bounds for the corresponding subsets. In a group with labels $(0,0,1)$, the global majority is 0. If the last node is the test subset, the function's assignment scores zero there, while the subset's best constant scores one. If the last node is instead the sole training node, a training-only majority predicts 1 and scores zero on the first two nodes; the all-label majority scores one on those two nodes. [Original checks](source_checks.py).

Aggregate purity can also conceal a small class's errors. Two groups containing three class-0 customers and one class-1 customer each have aggregate majority accuracy of 75%, with zero recall for class 1. This is an invented arithmetic illustration. It motivates reporting customer-group outcomes and selecting a loss function that reflects the decision.

## Outcomes Can Enter Before Model Fitting

The default `alpha=None` in [UGC](reference/algorithms/ugc.py) calculates its feature-versus-structure weight from the fraction of edges connecting different labels. The function reads `data.y` at both endpoints across all edges, including test-node labels. Its docstring states this choice explicitly. On a three-node path, changing only the last node's held-out label from 0 to 1 changes this fraction from zero to one-half when the other labels are zero. Preprocessing can therefore depend on the very outcomes later used for evaluation.

For a predictive exercise, choose a fixed alpha in advance or tune it using only the permitted training and validation information. Retain an untouched final evaluation sample. Access to test-node features in a transductive design is a separate choice from access to test-node outcomes.

[STPGC](reference/algorithms/stpgc.py) also has explicit label-guidance settings. Its default uses training and validation labels; `train_only` narrows the available information, and `label_guide=False` removes label guidance. The [cross-scoring script](reference/reproduce/cross_scoring.py) explicitly disables STPGC's guidance. Its imported extra arguments do not override UGC's alpha default. The benchmark should therefore be read with each method's information set visible, rather than treating every row as label-free.

These code paths are particularly useful for AI-assisted coding. A generated workflow can execute without an exception while evaluating an oracle label assignment or allowing outcomes to affect preprocessing. Students can trace inputs, transformations, and output definitions, then write a small independent counterexample before trusting an interpretation.

## Figure Descriptions and Reading Scope

Figure 1 on PDF page 11 shows an original 500-node stochastic-block graph with three communities and the coarsened graph from each method at requested reduction 0.70. Colors indicate community composition; node area increases with the number of original members. Some methods produce balanced groups, some concentrate large groups in one community, and others mix community labels. Four methods are tuned for this synthetic graph, as indicated in the caption. The panels display different achieved node counts. The image supports comparison of aggregation patterns under those inputs.

Table 4 on PDF page 25 lists four metrics and the achieved ratio for Cora and PubMed. Its ranking depends on the metric, and its reported failures remain part of the comparison. Both pages were inspected visually. The review covers the main construction and evaluation in §§1–5, Appendix B.4–B.5, the preprocessing discussion in Appendix D, and the selected implementation paths cited above. Other appendix derivations and all upstream algorithms have not been independently verified.

The original Python checks execute exact small calculations and comparisons of selected reported table entries. They do not execute GraCo, reproduce the benchmark, or establish performance on course datasets. # Compressing a Retail Network Without Changing the Decision

A retail chain wants a smaller representation of its service network. The chain needs both a revenue summary and the share of customers who can reach an available outlet within five minutes. The same compressed graph may support one quantity and misrepresent the other.

## Four Zones and Two Supernodes

Consider four invented zones A, B, C, and D with equal populations. They form a path. Travel takes four minutes from A to B, one minute from B to C, and four minutes from C to D. An available store is at D. Weekly zone revenues are 10, 10, 10, and 40 dollars. These deliberately small values provide a transparent calculation, with no estimated demand or observed customer behavior.

Group A, B, and C together, and retain D as the second supernode. Binary lifting and its pseudoinverse give mean revenues of 10 and 40. Reconstructing the original revenue feature is exact. The mean across the two supernodes is 25, while the population mean across four equal-sized zones is 17.50. Weighting the group means by sizes three and one restores that mean. The total is 70; adding group means gives 50.

For the graph calculation, define affinity as the reciprocal of edge travel minutes. The original affinities are $1/4$, $1$, and $1/4$. These units differ from minutes. Summing affinities between groups leaves one coarse edge with weight $1/4$, after removal of within-group edges. The revenue feature has the same combinatorial Dirichlet energy, 225, before and after this aggregation. This equality concerns the specified block-constant feature and graph quadratic form.

Interpreting the reciprocal coarse edge as a four-minute trip discards travel within the first supernode. The actual trip from A to D takes nine minutes. At a five-minute threshold, B, C, and D have access, so the original equal-population share is 75%. Treating every zone in the first supernode as four minutes away raises the apparent share to 100%. The feature reconstruction and its energy remain exact throughout. Preserving those quantities does not establish preservation of the route comparison.

The [complete Python calculation](source_checks.py) constructs the matrices, compares the energies, enumerates shortest paths, and checks the access counts. [Saved outputs](source_checks.json) retain the units and results. No source package or neural network is used.

## A Connection to the Existing Retail Case

The [existing retail-access example](../../03_Data_and_Code/Retail_Accessibility/README.md) supplies a separate population check. Its disconnected origin remains in the 800-person denominator. A largest-component filter would discard 150 people and raise known access from 68.75% to 84.62% with no improvement for any person. Students can identify the relevant GraCo default, explain the changed estimand, and propose a representation that retains the original population.

The restaurant snapshot provides observed locations and recorded availability, but it does not supply customer residences or preferences. A later empirical extension would retain that distinction, freeze the street extract, preserve route units, and compare access at original origins. Applying a generic graph reduction to minute-valued edges without a justified transformation would change their meaning.

## Prediction and AI-Assisted Coding

Use the three-node label example in [SOURCE_REVIEW.md](SOURCE_REVIEW.md) to distinguish a partition's oracle purity from a classifier fitted on permitted information. Ask students to trace the labels used in `max_acc`, UGC's alpha calculation, and STPGC's guidance. A final evaluation set remains untouched while choosing the representation and its hyperparameters.

A useful coding prompt specifies the observation unit, edge direction and units, original population, permitted outcomes, target number of groups, and required outputs. The assistant must report achieved compression, excluded nodes, group sizes, and separate numerical and predictive checks. The student then verifies a hand-worked case and inspects the relevant source functions. The [optional practice](../../07_Labs/Graph_Coarsening/README.md) includes this exercise. The two original course programs and nine independent checks have run; no live assistant or upstream program has been evaluated here.

## Figures and Placement

An editable TikZ figure shows the four-zone path beside the two-supernode representation. Use Illinois navy for original nodes, orange group boundaries, and explicit travel-time labels. Its lower panel compares 75% original access with the incorrect 100% coarse interpretation, while showing that feature reconstruction is exact. Labels and shapes should carry the distinction alongside color.

The explanation and complete code appear in M5 §5.24 and M7 §7.38. M4 §4.22 connects group weights to segment summaries, M2 §2.23 connects preprocessing to measurement, and M9 §9.18.2 examines service responsibilities. Sessions 7 and 11 use existing meeting blocks, with fifteen and five minutes respectively. The optional practice includes the M1 AI-assisted coding workflow and creates no graded requirement.

For advanced students, compare a small number of GraCo methods against a simple aggregation baseline and the uncompressed graph at comparable achieved sizes. Evaluate the decision outcome at the original nodes, preserve the information split, and record runtime and memory. The full seventeen-method benchmark requires a separate computing budget; the paper's graph metrics and runtime results provide background for choosing that comparison.

# Network Compression and Customer Decisions

A retailer groups service zones to reduce computation. The smaller graph preserves weekly zone revenues while losing travel within a group. A separate customer-service example distinguishes the labels available for fitting from the outcomes used to evaluate predictions.

The inputs and programs are original synthetic teaching examples, motivated by Antonin Joly's [GraCo paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01200v1) and [source repository](https://github.com/Antonin-J/graco). They contain no observed customers. The [source review](../../01_Resources/32_Graph_Coarsening/SOURCE_REVIEW.md) identifies the pinned implementation and its defaults. GraCo and its dependencies were not installed or executed, and no graph neural network was trained.

## Reproduction

Python 3.10 or later and its standard library are sufficient. Run from the repository root:

```bash
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Graph_Coarsening/compress_network.py
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Graph_Coarsening/evaluate_labels.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s 03_Data_and_Code/Graph_Coarsening -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

Both programs read [data/cases.json](data/cases.json) relative to their own location and replace their saved outputs in `results/`. No network, model account, random seed, or downloaded executable is needed. Calculations are deterministic. [The data dictionary](DATA_DICTIONARY.md) defines the separate populations, labels, units, and information splits. [Verification](VERIFICATION.md) records execution and independent checks; [the manifest](manifest.json) records file hashes and provenance.

## Results

| Comparison | Result |
|---|---|
| Four zones compressed to two groups | 50% node reduction; group sizes 3 and 1. |
| Weekly mean zone revenue | 17.50 dollars with original-zone weights; 25 with equal group weights. |
| Weekly total revenue | 70 dollars; sum of group means is 50. |
| Revenue reconstruction and energy | Zero squared reconstruction error; energy 225 before and after. |
| Five-minute access, 400 original people | 300/400 = 75%; naive coarse route reports 400/400 = 100%. |
| One group's labels 0, 0, 1 | Full-group oracle purity 2/3; global-majority and training-only test scores 1 and 0 on the two held-out zero labels. |
| Two groups with three routine and one specialist-service customer each | Six of eight correctly assigned; zero of two specialist needs detected. |
| Separate path, one held-out label changed | All-edge disagreement changes from 0 to 0.5; training-edge disagreement stays 0. |

[network.json](results/network.json), [zones.csv](results/zones.csv), and [labels.json](results/labels.json) retain the values. The figure sources are [the four-zone diagram](../../06_Lecture_Notes/figures/M05_graph_coarsening.tex) and [the information-set diagram](../../06_Lecture_Notes/figures/M07_graph_labels.tex). They describe the fixed published inputs; modifying the inputs requires updating figure labels before rebuilding course PDFs.

Binary lifting and the combinatorial graph convention are chosen explicitly. GraCo's default degree-normalized lifting has a different interpretation. Affinities are reciprocal minutes; a sum of affinities does not by itself define a travel route. The four-zone energy equality concerns the specified revenue feature. The label scores are finite calculations, with no claim about typical empirical performance.

# Inputs, Units, and Outputs

All values in `data/cases.json` are original synthetic teaching inputs. Node indices are zero-based. Each case is separate; their populations and training splits must not be combined.

## Four-Zone Retail Network

| Field | Meaning and Units |
|---|---|
| `zones` | Four zones A-D in fixed order. |
| `population` | People at each original origin; initially 100 per zone, total 400. |
| `weekly_zone_revenue_dollars` | Invented weekly total revenue for each zone, in dollars: 10, 10, 10, 40. |
| `group` | Contiguous group IDs 0 and 1; A-C enter group 0, D enters group 1. |
| `edges_minutes` | Undirected simple edges `[origin, destination, minutes]`; positive travel time. |
| `store_node` | Node 3, zone D, contains the one available outlet. |
| `access_threshold_minutes` | Inclusive five-minute threshold, with zero travel at the store's own origin. |

No nodes or people are excluded. Feature means weight original zones equally; access shares weight origins by people. Mean zone revenue differs from individual spending. Affinity is defined as the reciprocal of edge minutes. Binary membership, its averaging pseudoinverse, and combinatorial energy are used explicitly. Internal coarse self-loops are removed. Population changes affect access weights and do not automatically change the zone-revenue feature definition.

`results/zones.csv` retains one row per original zone: people, group, original and reconstructed revenue, original travel minutes, naive coarse minutes, and the two binary access indicators. `results/network.json` records group sizes, means, totals, reconstruction squared error, coarse affinities (per minute), reduction `1 - groups / original_zones`, and the two access shares. Energy has units dollars squared per minute for the weekly revenue feature.

## Label Cases

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `outcomes` | Three node labels 0, 0, 1 within one group. |
| `train_indices`, `test_indices` | Training node 2; test nodes 0 and 1. The training-only constant uses only node 2's outcome. |
| `alternative_test_indices` | A separate scoring subset containing node 2, used to compare a global majority with that subset's own ceiling. It is a separate split illustration. |
| `minority_groups` | Two groups, each with three routine-service labels 0 and one specialist-service label 1. Eight synthetic customers; two positive cases. |
| `parameter_edges` | Separate three-node path with two undirected edges, each counted once. |
| `parameter_training_indices`, `parameter_heldout_indices` | Permitted nodes 0 and 1; held-out node 2, separate from the purity example. |
| `parameter_labels_before`, `parameter_labels_after` | Only node 2 changes from 0 to 1. Training labels remain 0, 0. |

`results/labels.json` gives label choices, scoring counts, oracle purity, test scores, class-1 recall, and edge disagreement using all edges or only training-training edges. Majority ties choose the smaller numeric class. A training group with no labeled observations raises an error; an applied classifier would need a separately justified fallback. The all-label majority is an oracle diagnostic. The only fitted predictor in this example is a constant chosen from training labels.

## Background Sources

The review pins GraCo commit `19da8a6031dcf1803faa5723148b5975a5462af6` and Joly's paper version `2611.01200v1`. The published Cora metrics and the separate 800-person retail calculation remain in the [source review](../../01_Resources/32_Graph_Coarsening/SOURCE_REVIEW.md); they are not observations in this input file. Original licenses for source material remain in the resource collection. These course inputs and programs contain no copied publisher data or executable upstream code.

# Network Compression and Predictive Evidence

A retail manager wants faster analysis while preserving revenue accounting and service access. A customer-service manager wants a smaller graph that still identifies uncommon specialist needs. Evaluate the representation against each decision and state what information may be used to fit it.

This activity is public optional ungraded practice. It creates no submission deadline or course-wide AI-use rule. Read [M5 §5.24](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M05_Text_Social_and_Network_Analysis.md), [M7 §7.38](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md), and the [data dictionary](../../03_Data_and_Code/Graph_Coarsening/DATA_DICTIONARY.md).

## 1. Retain the Original Population

Run the two commands and independent tests in the [example README](../../03_Data_and_Code/Graph_Coarsening/README.md). Reproduce the mean revenue, total revenue, energy, travel times, and access counts by hand before interpreting the output. Explain why a zero feature-reconstruction error can coexist with a nine-minute trip represented as four minutes.

In a local copy of the input, change A's population from 100 to 700. Hold edge times, store availability, and group membership fixed. Predict the original access share and then calculate it. Restore the original population and set the threshold to four minutes. Explain which original origins cross the threshold. Finally assign every original zone its own group and check whether the two route calculations agree.

## 2. Follow the Labels

For the three labels 0, 0, 1, identify which outcome chooses the training-only constant and which outcomes choose the oracle majority. Write the denominator beside each score. Reassign the evaluation subset to the last node alone and explain why the global-majority score is below that subset's own optimal constant score.

In the separate parameter example, change only the held-out outcome. Compare disagreement using all edges and using training-training edges. Explain why final scored accuracy may change when reference labels change, while preprocessing and fitted predictions should remain invariant to outcomes that were forbidden during fitting.

For the two groups with one specialist customer each, calculate the confusion counts and class-1 recall. Propose a service loss that gives missed specialist needs an explicit cost, and state what evidence would justify that cost.

## 3. Inspect the Source Before Accepting Generated Code

Read the pinned [preprocessing](../../01_Resources/32_Graph_Coarsening/reference/loaders/preprocess.py), [label metric](../../01_Resources/32_Graph_Coarsening/reference/metrics/structural.py), and [UGC](../../01_Resources/32_Graph_Coarsening/reference/algorithms/ugc.py) functions. Identify the defaults controlling components, direction, label choice, and alpha. Use the [source review](../../01_Resources/32_Graph_Coarsening/SOURCE_REVIEW.md) to check the exact version and operator convention. Reading these files requires no dependency installation.

A coding request can specify: “Use the four synthetic zones and retain all original people. Keep travel minutes separate from graph affinities. Report achieved group count, group sizes, revenue means and totals, and access at every original origin. For prediction, use only the stated training labels to fit preprocessing and constants. Preserve untouched test outcomes. Add an independent path enumeration and a held-out-label intervention check.”

Compare the generated program with the requested objects and inspect every default that changes them. Record material AI assistance and distinguish code inspection from execution. A package call and a saved output do not establish that the claimed quantity was evaluated.

## 4. Recommend a Representation

Choose a primary customer outcome before comparing methods. State the original population, weights, target compression, achieved size, feature convention, label permissions, tuning budget, runtime, and memory. Use the uncompressed graph and a simple grouping baseline. Evaluate access or service errors at original nodes, including disconnected customers and uncommon needs.

Explain whether the computational saving justifies the observed errors and what would change the recommendation. Connect the affected customers' ability to obtain service or contest a decision to [M9 §9.18.2](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M09_Marketing_Dialectics.md). # Ontologies and Marketing Evidence

A marketing team needs a shared definition of a customer, purchase, cancellation, and consent before it can compare results across systems or ask an AI assistant to analyze them. An ontology makes categories, relationships, and inference rules explicit. Its value for this course is greatest when a plausible calculation conceals a disagreement about what the records mean.

The [Ontology Playground](https://learn-ontology.vercel.app/#learn) provides an accessible introduction through short lessons, editable graphs, and questions with reasoning traces. The strongest course adaptation is an exercise in specifying and challenging definitions. The [source review](SOURCE_REVIEW.md) separates the site's instructional ideas from the conditions needed for a reliable marketing application.

| --- | --- |

| M2: Customer Data and Measurement | Distinguish a missing record, a recorded zero, an inferred category, and an independently verified outcome |
| M5: Text and Networks | Represent a speaker's claim with its source, date, and scope; evaluate retrieval against the original passage |
| M9: Marketing Dialectics | Examine who chose a category and whether the inference from a commercial record to a customer right is justified |
| Future Wiki | Let students predict an inference, reveal its supporting facts, change an assumption, and compare the result |

# Definitions, Inference, and Evidence

## Instructional Design

The [site](https://learn-ontology.vercel.app/#learn) organizes six chapters around classes, individuals, relationships, chained rules, contradictions, and applications. Learners can choose everyday or technical examples. Its Detective section asks for a prediction before showing a proof, with an optional SQL explanation. The conflicting-revenue case was completed in the hosted interface: the displayed trace identifies two class assignments and the disjointness rule that makes their combination inconsistent.

For the course wiki, the useful design is a short cycle: state a managerial question, expose the inputs and rules, ask for a prediction, and reveal each inference with its source. Keep a text and table representation beside the graph. An original implementation can run locally in a static page and export the student's definitions in a readable format. Points and badges are optional; the source review supplies no estimate of their learning effect.

## Domain Rules and Data Validation

An OWL domain or range declaration can infer a type from a relationship. A missing type declaration does not automatically invalidate the relationship. Under OWL's open-world semantics, an absent fact can remain unknown. SHACL supplies a separate framework for testing whether an RDF graph satisfies declared conditions. These distinctions are explained in the [W3C OWL Primer, §§2 and 4.6](https://www.w3.org/TR/owl2-primer/) and [SHACL specification, §§1 and 4](https://www.w3.org/TR/shacl/).

Consider an original marketing rule: the range of `placedBy` is `Customer`. Recording that an order was placed by account A classifies A as a Customer under that rule. The inference does not verify the transaction, establish that the account belongs to one person, or determine whether the person authorized advertising. Those questions require additional evidence and explicit definitions. A generated analysis should retain the transaction source, account identifier, time, and relevant permission record.

Use ordinary Python or SQL checks for required timestamps, unique keys, allowed units, and missing values in the introductory exercise. Introduce SHACL as a possible implementation when the data are represented in RDF. A complete OWL reasoner is unnecessary for teaching these distinctions.

## Assess the Definitions Behind a Contradiction

The site's introductory examples often attribute contradictions to incorrect records. In a course application, evaluate the records and the axioms together. Declaring `LoyalCustomer` and `PriceSensitiveCustomer` disjoint creates an inconsistency when a customer belongs to both. The business meaning of these categories provides no general reason for that disjointness. Correcting the category definition may be more appropriate than deleting a customer observation.

The revenue case is useful when the object is a metric definition with an explicit refund convention. A gross-revenue measure and a net-revenue measure can also have identical numerical values when refunds are zero. Numerical equality does not make the definitions identical. Store the definition, currency, period, unit, and refund treatment alongside the value.

For time-varying states, identify the observation's date. A subscription can be active in one period and canceled in another without contradiction. Attach a state to an account-period or state interval, rather than making an account permanently belong to incompatible categories.

## Claims, Graphs, and AI Retrieval

An ontology defines vocabulary and rules. A knowledge graph records entities and relationships using a representation that may employ an ontology. A taxonomy supplies a category hierarchy. A database schema specifies the structure of stored records. These objects can work together; none alone establishes the truth of a statement extracted from a document.

For earnings calls, preserve an object such as `Claim` with a speaker, company, call date, source passage, and stated time horizon. A link saying that an executive attributes a price increase to input costs should remain an attributed assertion. Turning it into an unqualified causal relationship changes the evidence.

[Microsoft's GraphRAG documentation](https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/) describes a particular pipeline that extracts entities and relationships, builds communities, and produces summaries for retrieval. An OWL inference engine and that pipeline perform different tasks. The course can compare a small manually checked graph with text retrieval on the same questions, measuring source support, missing evidence, and cost. The presence of a graph is insufficient evidence of improved answer accuracy.

## Implementation and Reading Scope

The inspected [repository revision](https://github.com/mani-bellan/concept-playgrounds/tree/4fc52fd92f644e03e76880c5de16f0accb4770e7) is dated November 23, 2026. Its README, all six chapter definitions, and the complete small reasoner were read. Selected example definitions were inspected. The hosted overview, course menu, and conflicting-revenue Detective exercise were checked in the browser. The website's deployment commit was not exposed, so the hosted interface and pinned repository are recorded separately.

The [reasoner](https://github.com/mani-bellan/concept-playgrounds/blob/4fc52fd92f644e03e76880c5de16f0accb4770e7/ontology/src/ontology.js) applies subclass inheritance, domain, range, inverse, and transitive rules to a fixed point, then checks explicit disjoint class memberships. It preserves one derivation for each added fact. It implements an instructional subset of OWL: the code omits self-edges from transitive cycles and does not implement general OWL cardinality or datatype reasoning. Its Turtle exporter replaces non-alphanumeric characters with underscores; distinct names can therefore map to the same identifier. An original course implementation should use stable unique identifiers and test export separately.

No upstream source was installed or executed locally. The hosted exercise does not establish that every lesson, export, or browser interaction works. No repository-wide license was identified, so source files and lesson text are linked rather than redistributed. The [implemented marketing example](../../03_Data_and_Code/Ontology_and_Evidence/README.md) is an original course design with separately executed Python checks.

# Representation Quality and Marketing Decisions

A marketing analyst may compress customer information or use AI features to identify important complaints. ## Source: 01_Resources/34_Representation_Evaluation/SOURCE_REVIEW.md

# Reconstruction, Stability, and Interpretation

## Research Finding

Delisle and Tan study sparse autoencoders that reconstruct language-model activations. In affected settings, a dominant principal component can inflate overall reconstruction scores and make highly ranked features unstable across training seeds. Their Qwen-2.5-7B example explains 99.96% of total variance while leaving about 33% of variance outside PC1 unexplained. Their correction trains on the orthogonal component and restores PC1 during reconstruction. The paper reports improved reconstruction and top-feature reproducibility in affected models. Effects depend on the model, layer, preprocessing, and evaluation procedure. Its sparse-probe results also show that improved representation diagnostics need not produce large task-accuracy gains. See [version 1, §§3–7 and Appendices A, E, H](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.13548v1).

The course inference is to select an evaluation target from the managerial decision before relying on a convenient internal score. These experiments concern model activations; they do not estimate customer behavior, identify consumer motives, or establish a general correction for marketing datasets.

## What the Saved Results Measure

The archived [fidelity table](reference/results/additional/reconstruction/nine_model/nine_model_fidelity.csv) contains standard and bypass rows for nine models. Its provenance specifies 200,000 held-out WikiText-103 tokens, with the mean and PC1 obtained from the training store. There are three or five seeds per row. For Qwen-2.5-7B, the standard row has total fraction of variance unexplained (FVU) 0.00036992 and orthogonal FVU 0.329781. Calculating `100 * (1 - fvu_total)` gives 99.963008% total variance explained. Calculating `100 * fvu_content` gives 32.9781% orthogonal variance unexplained. These use different denominators.

The same table gives Qwen orthogonal FVU 0.217913 after bypass, a relative reduction of approximately 33.92%. The original calculation checks recompute these values from the archived table. They verify transformations of saved measurements; the activation-level experiment remains unexecuted.

The [feature summary](reference/results/tables/features_summary.csv) uses another comparison convention. Its `top50` column averages comparisons from reference seed 42 to four other seeds; `top50_allpairs` uses all 20 ordered comparisons. Qwen's standard/bypass `top50` values are 6% and 99.5%, while the all-pairs values are 6% and 96.8%. The fidelity table's corresponding sharing entries are 6% and 98% in its own smaller seed collection. Each number must travel with its file, seed set, selection rule, and denominator. Combining these columns into one purported replication would change the comparison.

## Evaluation Code Worth Reading

The archived [matching implementation](reference/experiments/language/pc1_v3/v3/common/matching.py) compares decoder directions using signed cosine similarity. Its default best-match comparison can use every direction in the other dictionary, while its dictionary-wide denominator includes alive features in the reference dictionary. A direction and its negation have different meanings when coefficients are nonnegative. An absolute-cosine comparison would change this metric. The file also provides mutual and one-to-one matching functions; the default best match is a different correspondence rule.

The [loading and reconstruction implementation](reference/pc1_sae/__init__.py) centers each activation with the saved training mean, projects onto a saved PC1 direction, encodes the remainder, and restores the projection during decoding. It requires the preprocessing assets for the matching checkpoint and layer. Deleting the leading component from an ordinary customer dataset would be a different operation. That component may carry business-relevant information.

The [experiment guide](reference/experiments/README.md) separates training, evaluation, probing, behavioral edits, and explanation scoring. The [requirements](reference/requirements-models.txt) and loader show that reproducing the models requires a substantial environment and checkpoint access. The small course example can establish the mathematical issue without these dependencies.

## An Original Decision Example

To see what determines an aggregate reconstruction score, split a centered input into a leading direction and its orthogonal remainder. Let $V_1$ and $V_{\perp}$ be their squared variation in the evaluation sample, and let $E_1$ and $E_{\perp}$ be the corresponding squared reconstruction errors. Orthogonality gives

$$
\frac{E_1+E_{\perp}}{V_1+V_{\perp}}
=w_1\frac{E_1}{V_1}+(1-w_1)\frac{E_{\perp}}{V_{\perp}},
\qquad w_1=\frac{V_1}{V_1+V_{\perp}}.
$$

The left side is total FVU. Each component error on the right is weighted by its share of variation; both component denominators must be positive. When the leading direction is reconstructed exactly, the remaining component's error receives weight $1-w_1$. A small weight can make that error almost invisible in the aggregate. The example below makes all of these quantities observable by construction.

Consider four equally weighted, invented centered representations of complaint text: `(-100, -1)`, `(-100, 1)`, `(100, -1)`, and `(100, 1)`. The first coordinate represents a large document-style component by construction. The second represents a complaint distinction used to route a case for review; a positive value requires review. These meanings are imposed for the illustration.

Representation A preserves the first coordinate and replaces the second with zero. It explains approximately 99.9900% of total squared variation, while missing both cases that require review. Representation B multiplies the first coordinate by 0.98 and preserves the second. It explains approximately 99.9600% of total variation and routes both review cases correctly. The aggregate reconstruction ranking therefore reverses the ranking for the chosen decision. The [original program](source_checks.py) verifies the arithmetic and reports the denominators.

This calculation requires no claim about what a real model's first component means. A practical adaptation would use a manually checked complaint set, fit transformations using training data, and evaluate held-out routing performance and customer-group outcomes. The observed task performance would decide whether a proposed preprocessing change is helpful.

## Feature Importance and a Unique Explanation

Two different decompositions can reconstruct the same vector. In an original two-dimensional illustration, unit directions proportional to `(1, 1)` and `(1, -1)`, each with coefficient `sqrt(2)`, sum to `(2, 0)`. Directions proportional to `(1, 2)` and `(1, -2)`, each with coefficient `sqrt(5)`, produce the same result. Removing one term leaves a large error in either representation. The size of that error alone does not select a unique underlying concept.

This is an exact algebraic counterexample, not a trained SAE or an estimated marketing mechanism. Its teaching role is to separate sensitivity to an intervention on a representation from the substantive meaning assigned to a feature. Feature stability, prediction, and human interpretation need their own evidence. For a segmentation application, compare customer assignments and label-aligned descriptions across runs rather than treating a cluster number as a stable behavioral type.

## Review Scope and Rights

The review covers the paper's main evaluation and repair arguments, selected appendix definitions, and 13 repository files at commit `a3df7fff7a3f03012a116cbd092d2a24f2941e64`, dated November 10, 2026. The arXiv record identifies the paper as accepted at NeurIPS 2026. That publication-status statement comes from the record; no independent conference-program check was performed.

The repository licenses code under MIT and results under CC BY 4.0. Both notices are preserved. The paper uses the arXiv perpetual non-exclusive license and is linked rather than republished. The source subset is incomplete and is provided for inspection. No upstream script, dependency installation, checkpoint download, model training, model inference, or LLM evaluator was executed. The original standard-library checks cover the archived-file hashes, saved-result calculations, and two invented mathematical illustrations.

# Cancellation Records and Customer Evidence

A subscription manager needs to identify cancellation requests that require review and report recorded cancellations at a fixed date. Treating a request as a completed cancellation changes both outputs. The original synthetic case distinguishes customer accounts, subscriptions, events, and dated state observations.

## Inputs and Execution

`data/cancellation_records.json` contains four subscriptions and eight event rows, assessed at January 31, 2027, 23:59 UTC. All identifiers, dates, and records are invented. Python 3.10 or later and its standard library are sufficient. Run from the repository root:

```bash
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Ontology_and_Evidence/assess_cancellations.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s 03_Data_and_Code/Ontology_and_Evidence -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

The program resolves exact duplicates, rejects conflicting copies, validates event references and timestamps, excludes information after the cutoff, and checks confirmation chronology. It writes `results/cancellations.json`. The population denominator remains all four subscriptions. A request without an accepted confirmation enters a review queue; this is a search over the supplied records and does not establish that cancellation failed outside those records.

## Results and Interpretation

Four unique events remain. One extra duplicate, one missing timestamp, one later confirmation, and one confirmation preceding its request account for the other four rows. There are two valid requests, of which `r1` needs review. One of four subscriptions has a latest accepted cancellation confirmation. Counting requests as completions reports two of four. The dated active observation for `s3` and the unknown state of `s4` remain distinct.

[M1 §1.16 and M2 §2.25](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M02_Customer_Data_and_Visualization.md) connect definitions, rule-based classification, data validation, and evidence. Full Python appears in M2. The [optional lab](../../07_Labs/Ontology_and_Evidence/README.md) changes cutoffs and challenges claims. The script implements explicit Python conditions; it is not an OWL reasoner or a SHACL implementation.

## Provenance and Verification

The original case is informed by the [ontology source review](../../01_Resources/33_Ontologies_and_Knowledge_Representation/README.md), the [W3C OWL 2 Primer](https://www.w3.org/TR/owl2-primer/), and [SHACL](https://www.w3.org/TR/shacl/). No playground source was copied. See the [dictionary](DATA_DICTIONARY.md), [agent guide](AGENTS.md), [verification record](VERIFICATION.md), and [manifest](manifest.json).

# Cancellation Evidence Dictionary

All inputs are synthetic. The observation unit in the roster is a subscription; the event file may contain repeated event rows. Counts of requests, events, accounts, and subscriptions have different denominators.

| Field | Meaning and Units |
| --- | --- |
| `synthetic` | True identifies invented inputs. |
| `cutoff` | Inclusive reporting cutoff, ISO timestamp with UTC offset. |
| `subscription_id` | Unique subscription identifier; the complete reporting population has four entries. |
| `account_id` | Invented customer account attached to a subscription. No person-level identity is claimed. |
| `event_id` | Event identifier; exact copies collapse to one, conflicting copies are all rejected. |
| `kind` | `request`, `confirmation`, or `active_observation`. |
| `at` | Recorded event time with UTC offset; null fails the timestamp requirement. |
| `request_id` | A confirmation's reference to an accepted request for the same subscription. |
| `evidence_state` | Latest accepted confirmation or active observation, simultaneous conflict, request without confirmation, or unknown. |
| `state_observed_at` | Time of the latest accepted state observation; null when no such observation exists. |
| `requests_to_review` | Accepted requests without an accepted confirmation by the cutoff. |
| `flags[].rows` | Number of raw rows accounted for by a flag. Extra duplicate rows are flagged separately from the retained event. |
| `classification_trace` | Explicit mapping of each accepted event kind to a modeled class and the common parent `ServiceRecord`. |
| `confirmed_share` | Subscriptions whose latest accepted state is a cancellation confirmation divided by all roster subscriptions. |
| `request_as_completion_share` | Subscriptions with any accepted request divided by all roster subscriptions; deliberately misleading completion measure. |

The latest accepted state describes available records. A later unobserved event may change the actual state. Null timing prevents an event from entering the cutoff comparison. Event types are operational modeling choices, not verified evidence of consent, legal compliance, or actual service execution.

# Representation Quality and Customer Decisions

A service manager choosing a text representation needs to retain the information that identifies cases for review. Total reconstruction quality weights errors by variation, which can be concentrated in a different component. A second case examines whether exact reconstruction identifies a unique feature interpretation.

## Inputs and Execution

All vectors and labels are invented. `data/cases.json` has four equally weighted cases, two style scales, and a fixed shrinkage factor. Python 3.10 or later and the standard library are sufficient. Run from the repository root:

```bash
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Representation_Evaluation/evaluate_representations.py
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Representation_Evaluation/compare_decompositions.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s 03_Data_and_Code/Representation_Evaluation -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

The first program writes `results/representations.json`, including input vectors, reconstruction errors, variance weights, and routing metrics. The second writes `results/decompositions.json`, including unit directions, coefficients, reconstructed vectors, and removal errors. No dependencies, model downloads, random seed, or network access are required.

## Results and Scope

At style scale 100, representation A explains 99.990001% of variation and recalls none of the two review-required cases. B explains 99.960004% and recalls both. At style scale 1, their explained shares are 50% and 99.98%; the routing results stay the same. Coordinate units reverse the reconstruction ranking. The fixed evaluation labels define the routing target; they are not used to train or select a model here.

Two pairs of weighted unit directions both sum to `(2, 0)`. Removing the first contribution produces squared reconstruction errors of 2 and 5. The coefficient sums differ, so equal reconstruction does not imply equal sparse-autoencoder objectives. Neither calculation estimates a feature's psychological meaning or causal role.

Full Python and three comparisons appear in [M7 §§7.39–7.40](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M07_Prediction_and_Machine_Learning.md). See the [dictionary](DATA_DICTIONARY.md), [agent guide](AGENTS.md), [verification](VERIFICATION.md), and [optional lab](../../07_Labs/Representation_Evaluation/README.md).

## Sources

The [review of Delisle and Tan](../../01_Resources/34_Representation_Evaluation/README.md) motivates separate evaluation of aggregate reconstruction, component errors, feature stability, and task outcomes. Their experiments concern internal model activations. The course examples use fixed transformations of invented vectors to compare reconstruction and decision metrics. Sparse-autoencoder training and empirical customer outcomes require separate data and estimation. Attribution and licenses for the separately archived source subset are retained in the resource folder.

## Source: 03_Data_and_Code/Representation_Evaluation/DATA_DICTIONARY.md

# Representation Evaluation Dictionary

Every numerical input is synthetic. The four cases receive equal weight. Coordinates are imposed standardized scores except that the first is multiplied by a stated scale; no text embeddings were estimated.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `case_id` | Unique case identifier. |
| `style_sign` | Imposed style score, −1 or +1. |
| `review_signal` | Imposed review score, −1 or +1. Review is required when positive. |
| `style_scales` | Multipliers 100 and 1 on the first coordinate. |
| `representation_B_style_multiplier` | Fixed factor 0.98. A preserves the first coordinate and sets the second to zero; B shrinks the first and preserves the second. |
| `variation` | Sum of squared deviations from each coordinate's mean over the four evaluation cases. |
| `squared_errors` | Sum of squared reconstruction errors by coordinate. |
| `component_fvu` | Coordinate squared error divided by its variation. |
| `variance_weights` | Coordinate variation divided by total variation. |
| `total_fvu` | Total squared reconstruction error divided by total variation. |
| `variance_explained_pct` | 100 times one minus total FVU; this measure may be negative for poor reconstructions. |
| `recall` | Correctly routed positive cases divided by the two cases requiring review. |
| `accuracy` | Correct binary routing decisions divided by all four cases. |
| `unit_directions` | Two Euclidean-unit vectors in each imposed decomposition. |
| `coefficient_per_direction` | Positive weight multiplying each direction, square root of 2 or 5. |
| `contributions` | Weighted directions, `(1, ±1)` or `(1, ±2)`. |
| `squared_error_after_removing_first` | Squared Euclidean distance from target `(2, 0)` to the remaining contribution. |

FVU uses coordinate-specific units and an orthonormal coordinate system. A change of units changes its relative penalties. Routing metrics preserve the same case population and reference labels. The examples have no train/test fit; a learned system would require an independently held-out evaluation and training-only preprocessing.

# Agent Workflow Evaluation

An AI-generated analysis can fail because of its calculation, supplied information, available tools, execution environment, or checker. This collection connects those possibilities to a controlled comparison of coding workflows and to the cost of obtaining a valid analysis.

## Reading and Original Applications

Li and coauthors' [Agent Harness Engineering: A Survey](LiXiaoZhangLiuEtAl_WorkingPaper2026.pdf) organizes execution, tools, context, orchestration, observability, evaluation, and governance. Read §8 for task definition, environment readiness, execution records, separate judgments of outputs and actions, and evaluation of the checker itself. Sections 5 and 11 connect persistent context and interacting components to workflow design. Section 9 discusses authority and enforcement.

- [Source review](SOURCE_REVIEW.md): evidence, scope, companion repository, and rights.
- [Original case design](CASE_DESIGN.md): managerial question, information-by-feedback experiment, and interpretation.
- [Course example](../../03_Data_and_Code/Agent_Workflows/README.md): actual mHealth logging calculations, independent tests, and hypothetical cost comparison.
- [Optional ungraded lab](../../07_Labs/Agent_Workflows/README.md): guided checks and an optional measured model comparison.
- [Catalog](catalog.json) and [manifest](manifest.json): versioned source information.

The paper's figures include a seven-layer taxonomy and a five-stage evaluation cycle. The course adaptation uses original editable TikZ diagrams for the factorial design and the difference between matching an aggregate and assigning values to the correct customers. This Markdown guide summarizes selected arguments; it is not a complete transcription of the 71-page survey.

## Source: 01_Resources/35_Agent_Workflow_Evaluation/SOURCE_REVIEW.md

# Execution Systems and Evidence

## Research Scope

Li and coauthors define an agent harness as the infrastructure that turns model calls into bounded, stateful execution through tools, information management, orchestration, monitoring, verification, and governance. Their survey describes 171 catalog entries and a filtered technical map of 138 artifacts. Section 2 reports a May 8, 2026 metadata snapshot and a single primary coder with author review. The public, English-language, GitHub-visible coding ecosystem is overrepresented. Category counts describe selected artifacts and their documented functions; they do not measure deployment shares or causal benefits.

Section 8 treats performance as a property of a model operating within a specified system. It distinguishes task grounding, readiness checks, controlled execution, outcome and action evaluation, evaluation of the grader, and subsequent regression checks. A recorded failure can motivate a diagnosis. Identifying the contribution of a component requires controlled variation or other credible identification. The course's four-cell protocol varies explicit context and development feedback at a fixed model version.

Sections 5 and 11 support selective information retrieval, durable task state, and evaluation after component changes. These are design questions to assess on relevant tasks. Claims about a particular context length, tool, product, or model need their own dated evidence. The course does not reproduce the survey's secondary benchmark magnitudes as measured marketing productivity gains.

## Companion Repository

The reviewed [awesome-agent-harness repository](https://github.com/Picrew/awesome-agent-harness/tree/e7e8f8d268f7ac5311b778832327e4be2f555507) is a curated directory. Its README reports 375 entries and nine categories. Its curation and verification documents describe a YAML source, generated language mirrors, required fields, duplicate checks, activity checks, and URL reachability. Inspection of `scripts/verify_catalog.py` confirms that it checks catalog structure and links. It does not run the listed agents or establish their performance. No repository script was executed.

The current repository's 375 entries and the paper's 138 retained artifacts refer to different collections and snapshots. Neither count establishes quality. No repository-wide license was identified at the reviewed commit, so the course retains original annotations and links rather than a copied source tree.

## Philosophical Application

The survey's governance discussion concerns permissions, identities, controls, and accountability. The course extends it to the justification of marketing objectives. A cancellation agent may obey a firm's instructions while frustrating a customer's expressed wish to leave. Kantian respect for persons raises the question of whether the procedure respects the customer's capacity to form and act on reasons. The Confucian discussion connects the role of a cancellation service to its conduct. These applications are original course interpretations, distinct from an empirical finding of the survey.

## Source Access and Rights

OpenReview's forum and PDF routes returned a browser-verification page during review. The paper was read from the author-hosted Hugging Face dataset at revision `cbdb25e65f27874077a906b95b5746f0642e9551`. That dataset contains a PDF, not a benchmark dataset. # A Valid Customer-Activity Report

## Managerial Decision

A manager wants to identify customers whose recorded logging has declined before deciding whether an outreach study is warranted. The measurement must retain the earlier roster, count distinct dates in a specified window, and preserve customers without later records. Actual mHealth observations establish the logging table. They do not identify a response to outreach or a health benefit.

## Comparison

Cross an explicit data dictionary with executable development feedback while holding the model, task, tools, permissions, and resource caps fixed. The four conditions separate each contribution and their interaction. Five clean-session repetitions per cell provide a feasible classroom protocol for variation on the fixed task. July supports development; August evaluates the frozen program. Student teams must keep evaluation answers out of the model workspace during a measured comparison.

The original programs supply a verified reference, a CSV grader, independent boundary and denominator tests, and a separately calculated SQL result. A synthetic A/B/C case shows that equal total logged days can assign activity to the wrong customer. This motivates checking the checker against decision-relevant errors. No measured four-cell results are supplied.

## Costs and Customer Authority

A separate hypothetical example compares total model charges and analyst effort across 100 assigned tasks. The higher-API-cost workflow has lower total cost under the stated review and correction inputs. Failed attempts remain in the cost numerator and assigned-task denominator. These inputs illustrate the accounting comparison; they do not estimate an AI productivity effect.

The cancellation discussion separates valid execution, company authorization, customer authorization, and ethical justification. A technically successful retention procedure can frustrate an explicit cancellation request. Students should assess the customer's reasons and the firm's means before ranking commercial performance.

## Placement

M1 §1.17 supplies the workflow definitions and complete reference code. M6 §6.29 defines the factorial contrast. M7 §7.41 connects customer-level grading, checker errors, and repeated evaluation. M8 §8.26 supplies the cost calculation. M9 §9.20 develops authority and justification. Sessions 1, 9, 11, and 14 use existing discussion blocks; the longer experiment remains optional ungraded practice. The course remains 15 meetings of 170 minutes.

# AI Workflow Evaluation

A manager needs a reproducible measure of recorded customer activity before selecting an outreach population. The mHealth tasks calculate logging days for a roster fixed using earlier records. An original factorial protocol varies the information and feedback supplied to a coding assistant while holding its model fixed.

## Run the Local Calculations

Use Python 3.11 or newer with the standard library. Run from the repository root:

```sh
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Agent_Workflows/logging_reference.py
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Agent_Workflows/workflow_costs.py
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Agent_Workflows/test_workflows.py
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Agent_Workflows/evaluate_submission.py 03_Data_and_Code/Agent_Workflows/results/development_reference.csv
```

The compact task inputs are included. To recreate them from the existing public mHealth release, first follow its [download instructions](../mHealth/README.md), then run `python3 03_Data_and_Code/Agent_Workflows/build_tasks.py`. The builder verifies the compressed source checksum and reads it once. It makes no network requests and exports no food descriptions, weight fields, ages, or original identifiers.

## Inputs and Outputs

- [Data dictionary](DATA_DICTIONARY.md): units, dates, eligibility, and field definitions.
- [Task manifest](manifest.json): source checksum, selection, row counts, and input hashes.
- [Reference results](results/README.md): observed counts and their interpretation.
- [Experiment protocol](EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL.md): four configurations, run records, costs, and evaluation separation.
- [Optional ungraded lab](../../07_Labs/Agent_Workflows/README.md): guided calculations and controlled errors.
- [Verification record](VERIFICATION.md): local execution and independent checks.

The saved logging results are calculations from transformed real mHealth records. Cost scenarios use explicitly hypothetical inputs. Published model results are separately attributed to the authors of the coding benchmark. No model was called for the course, no empirical comparison of the four AI configurations was run, and no upstream repository code was executed. A correctly generated CSV checks a measurement; it does not establish a nutrition or health outcome.

## Coding Workflows and Undetected Errors

`benchmark_evidence.py` reads three unchanged CC0 aggregate tables from [the source collection](../../01_Resources/40_Econometric_Coding_Workflows/README.md). It reconstructs 43,200 assigned runs, failure denominators, prompt contrasts, and token cost per additional success. The authors' original model runs, scoring, and bootstrap are not repeated.

`semantic_checks.py` applies eight original correct or deliberately incorrect programs to each mHealth task. It compares execution, complete roster output, total-day agreement, and per-user numerical agreement. The shifted-user case preserves July's 6,455 days and 58.16% mean while changing 331 users' values. These cases are designed counterexamples, not a measured distribution of model errors.

`decision_costs.py` compares 1,000 hypothetical analysis tasks with explicitly supplied API charges, review effort, undetected-error probabilities, and conditional losses. The checked workflow breaks even at a loss of seven dollars per undetected error. `build_coding_figures.py` writes two editable TikZ files from the corresponding numerical tables; the note builder renders them.

Full programs appear in M1 §1.19, M7 §7.46, and M8 §8.30. M3 §3.18 and M6 §6.31 connect uncertainty checks and interaction scales. The longer exercise remains optional and ungraded.

## Source: 03_Data_and_Code/Agent_Workflows/DATA_DICTIONARY.md

# Logging Tasks and Measurement

## Population and Timing

The source is the transformed mHealth teaching release dated October 23, 2026. Select public pseudonyms whose first four hexadecimal digits represent an integer below 4096, matching the recurring course cohort. Eligibility then requires at least one food record from January 1 through June 30, 2016. Both later tasks retain this same roster. Its membership reflects prior recorded activity, not an account-enrollment registry or a representative consumer sample.

July is the development task and August is the evaluation task. A task's start date is included and its end date is excluded. The input also contains the preceding date and the end date when observed, so filtering has an observable consequence. Local calendar dates are preserved from the source; no timestamp or time-zone interpretation is added.

## Files and Variables

| File or Field | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| `roster.csv`, `user_id` | One row for each eligible user. Aliases U0001 onward follow sorted public pseudonyms; the same alias identifies the same user in both tasks. |
| `observed_days.csv` | One row per observed user-date in the task window and its two boundary dates, restricted to the fixed roster. |
| `date` | ISO calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `entries` | Number of source food rows on that date. Several entries still represent one logged day. This is not calorie intake. |
| `task.json` | Task ID, included start, excluded end, and earlier eligibility cutoff. |
| `logged_days` | Distinct dates with at least one record in the specified window for this user. |
| `window_days` | Number of calendar days from included start to excluded end. |
| `logging_rate` | `logged_days / window_days`, on a 0–1 scale. |

Users without records during the task window remain in the output with zero logged days. That zero describes the released file's logging indicator. It does not establish zero food intake, account closure, or observation of every actual logging event. No nutrition screen is applied because the target is record presence rather than dietary intake.

## Controlled Errors

The independent tests use invented users A, B, C, and Z. They introduce a repeated date, a duplicate roster key, boundary dates, an out-of-roster record, an ambiguous non-ISO date, missing output users, and nonfinite values. These records remain separate from the actual mHealth task inputs. The reference calculation rejects duplicate roster keys and invalid dates; repeated event dates are collapsed to a distinct-day indicator.

## Published Benchmark Aggregates

The three CSVs under `01_Resources/40_Econometric_Coding_Workflows/data` retain the authors' schema. `appendix_silent_vs_loud.csv` contains three workflow rows. `n` counts assigned runs; `failures = loud + silent`. Fields ending in `per100` divide by assigned runs, whereas `silent_share_of_failures_pct` divides by failures. The `_lo` and `_hi` fields are supplied 95% percentile intervals from 4,000 bootstrap draws over 40 tasks.

`prompt_agency.csv` contains six prompt rows and nine platform rows, distinguished by `panel`. The stored `few_shot` label means one related code example in this manuscript. Each prompt cell has 7,200 assigned runs; each language cell has 4,800. `successes` is an integer count, and `success_pct` uses a 0–100 scale. The course contrast program selects the prompt panel explicitly.

`summary_by_model.csv` contains six model rows. Success fields ending in `_pct` use a 0–100 scale; cost fields ending in `_usd` are dollars. The incremental-cost calculation divides the difference in mean token cost per run by the difference in success probabilities on a 0–1 scale. It excludes analyst effort and downstream losses. Model names and effort levels remain the authors' labels.

## Constructed Error Assessments and Hypothetical Costs

`semantic_checks.csv` has one row per constructed program and period. `executed` records whether the program returned; `complete` requires every roster user and a finite value for each requested numeric field. `total_days_matches` checks only the sum of logged days. `valid` also checks every user's values against the reference. `mean_returned_rate` averages the rows returned by that program and can change its denominator or units in an incorrect case. Empty values are unavailable outcomes.

`decision_costs.csv` reports expected dollars for the stated number of assigned analyses. The probability of an undetected error is per assigned analysis; the loss is conditional on such an error reaching a decision. Review minutes include correction effort. All operating inputs are hypothetical and are recorded in `decision_cost_summary.json`.

# Agent Guide for Workflow Evaluation

Read README.md, DATA_DICTIONARY.md, and EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL.md before using these tasks. The root course guide and current assignment rules govern student assistance.

- Preserve the prior-period roster, half-open date interval, distinct-day unit, and zero-log users. Recorded logging is not food intake or an account-enrollment measure.
- Keep actual task calculations separate from invented test cases and hypothetical cost inputs.
- Published benchmark aggregates are attributed to Galiani, López, and Sosa. The course's constructed errors and hypothetical costs contain no newly measured LLM performance. Never present either optional model-comparison protocol as an executed experiment.
- Do not expose final evaluation answers during a measured model comparison. Restrict the task workspace explicitly; public filenames are not an access boundary.
- The CSV checker reads data only. It does not authorize or isolate generated-code execution. Review permissions and commands before a separately requested run.
- The task builder reads the existing local mHealth release and verifies its hash. It does not upload records to an external service.
- Maintain full Python blocks in the notes when changing their matching programs. Run the independent checks and preserve source and input hashes.
- Preserve assigned-run and conditional-failure denominators. The supplied benchmark intervals resample tasks; aggregate reconstruction does not rerun that bootstrap.

## Source: 03_Data_and_Code/Agent_Workflows/EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL.md

# Information, Feedback, and Coding Performance

## Decision and Four Configurations

Estimate whether explicit measurement information and executable development feedback improve a fixed model's ability to produce the required logging table. Cross two factors: a concise data dictionary (absent/present) and development-check feedback (absent/present). The four cells are basic instructions, information, feedback, and information plus feedback. Keep the task, output schema, model version, available execution tools, permissions, and maximum time and token budgets fixed. Record any provider behavior that prevents these controls from being held constant.

All cells receive the same core request: “Write a Python program that reads roster.csv, observed_days.csv, and task.json and produces one row per roster user with user_id, logged_days, window_days, and logging_rate. Count distinct recorded days inside the task interval, retain users with no records, and preserve the inputs. Return the complete program and its run command.” The information cells additionally receive the field definitions and timing rules in DATA_DICTIONARY.md. Redundancy is intentional: the experiment tests whether explicit structured context improves implementation of the same target.

Provide the schema and the synthetic A/B/C development case from the lab to the assistant. Execute generated code locally after inspecting it. The actual mHealth records remain local. In feedback cells, return the development check's observed discrepancies and permit at most two revisions within the common resource cap. In cells without feedback, permit the same code-execution access and budget, but withhold the independent check. Record actual utilization and any voluntarily performed checks.

## Development and Evaluation

Use July for development. Freeze instructions, tool descriptions, checker version, correction policy, and candidate code before scoring August. Evaluate the frozen program locally against the separately maintained reference. The evaluation files and expected answers are public course materials; conceal them from the model during a measured exercise through an explicitly restricted task workspace. A folder name alone supplies no isolation. The supplied CSV grader never executes submitted programs and implements no sandbox.

Repeat each configuration five times with fresh conversations and clean output directories. Randomize cell order within each repetition, record the order and model seed where supported, and keep model configuration fixed. Preserve each assigned attempt, including timeouts and missing outputs. Multiple runs of the August task measure variation on that task; they do not supply a sample of independent business problems. Broader generalization requires additional task families and a separate final evaluation set. A version change restarts the comparison or becomes an explicitly varied factor.

## Run Record and Outcomes

Record task and repetition IDs, configuration, model/version, prompt and input hashes, tool versions, exposed files, budgets, start/end times, generated program, executed commands, tool errors, feedback, revisions, final output hash, checker result, actual API charges, review minutes, correction minutes, and permission violations. Record an unavailable cost as missing. Retain visible actions and evidence; an assistant's explanation is not a direct observation of its internal reasoning.

The primary outcome is a valid complete table per assigned attempt. Also report user-level discrepancies, zero-log omissions, date-boundary errors, failed attempts, elapsed time, and human effort. A permission violation remains a separate outcome even when the table is correct. Check results with a separately written SQL calculation and the small cases. Equal overall totals can conceal errors assigned to different users.

For each cell, divide valid outputs by all assigned attempts. Sum model, execution, review, and correction costs across all attempts, including failures, before dividing by the number of valid outputs. If no output is valid, report that ratio as undefined. Report unresolved attempts alongside cost. Paired contrasts across repetitions preserve the common task; uncertainty describes repeat-run variation conditional on this task and model configuration.

The interaction is the information effect with feedback minus the information effect without feedback. It describes complementarity for the chosen outcome. Correct diagnosis requires controlled interventions: an execution record can locate a likely error without proving which component caused it. Re-evaluate the whole workflow after changing a model, prompt, data dictionary, tool, or checker.

## Separate Comparison of Three Coding Workflows

The [econometric coding study](../../01_Resources/40_Econometric_Coding_Workflows/README.md) motivates a second optional comparison. Keep it separate from the four-cell information-by-feedback design. Use a common core task statement, output schema, model version, software, and instruction to perform an independent numerical check. Vary how execution and revision occur:

| Condition | Procedure |
| --- | --- |
| Single Script | Obtain one complete program; execute it locally once and retain all output. Return no execution feedback. |
| Repair | Execute the initial program; return the exit status and missing-output information after a failure, allowing up to three revisions. Do not reveal reference numbers. |
| Agent | Permit local execution and revision on synthetic practice files within a common resource cap; let the agent declare completion. Retain its checks and commands. |

Use invented practice records for live model interaction. The fixed mHealth inputs and final expected answers stay outside the model's permitted workspace. Inspect generated code, then evaluate its frozen version locally on those records without sending them to an external service. This course design therefore evaluates local transfer to the actual measurement task; it is not an exact replication of the authors' supplied-data benchmark.

Predefine output completeness and numerical correctness separately. The supplied constructed-error exercise requires a row for every roster user and all finite requested fields. A complete but incorrect row contributes to a silent failure; missing users or requested values contribute to incomplete output. Also report which checks detect each error. An implausible range can expose a silent error even when execution supplies no warning.

Use fresh conversations, clean directories, and randomized condition order. Repeat over several synthetic task families before making claims about tasks in general. Preserve all assigned attempts and report actual expenditure, elapsed time, revisions, human review, and model versions. A single successful run does not determine a workflow's success probability. With shared tasks, compare conditions within tasks and retain task groups in uncertainty calculations.

The published agent condition also adds a verification instruction, whereas this course comparison holds that instruction constant. Record the distinction when interpreting results. If comparing prompts, report both the percentage-point gain and the fraction of baseline failures removed. Neither optional model comparison has been executed in the released course examples.
