[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2288-13-117); [university copy](https://pure-oai.bham.ac.uk/ws/files/16708327/Gale_Using_framework_method_BMC_Medical_Research_Methodology_2013.pdf) | Stages 2–7: familiarization, coding, analytical framework, indexing, charting, and interpretation | Adapt a case-by-category matrix to public documents. Preserve each issuer's context and compare related claims before comparing issuers. The original application emphasizes interviews; this document-based adaptation is a course design choice. |
| O'Connor, C., and H. Joffe (2020). “Intercoder Reliability in Qualitative Research: Debates and Practical Guidelines.” *International Journal of Qualitative Methods*, 19. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1177/1609406919899220); [author repository](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/10091273/) | Practical considerations for evaluating a shared coding frame | Independently code a subset, inspect disagreements, revise definitions, and preserve original judgments. An agreement statistic would assess application of the coding frame, not the truth of an executive's assertion. |
| Braun, V., and V. Clarke (2021; published online 2020). “One Size Fits All? What Counts as Quality Practice in (Reflexive) Thematic Analysis?” *Qualitative Research in Psychology*, 18(3), 328–352. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1080/14780887.2020.1769238); [author repository](https://uwe-repository.worktribe.com/output/6631950/one-size-fits-all-what-counts-as-quality-practice-in-reflexive-thematic-analysis) | Methodological coherence and the limits of universal coding-reliability requirements | Identify this exercise as directed content analysis with a codebook. Do not treat its agreement procedure as a requirement for every form of qualitative research. |

# Utility Disclosures and Household Costs

A household advocate must assess whether an assurance about electricity affordability addresses infrastructure cost recovery. The example retrieves public disclosures, identifies passages for contextual reading, and compares claims about investment, customer charges, and revenue offsets. The resulting evidence establishes institutional mechanisms and stated plans. A data-center-specific causal effect requires a separate empirical comparison.

## Inputs and Reproduction

The purposeful selection contains six documents from five issuer families, including three earnings calls. Ten course-authored paraphrases retain speakers, locators, populations, evidence stages, counterevidence, and interpretation limits. These are assistant-prepared annotations checked against sources, with independent human coding pending. Counts describe the selection. They do not estimate prevalence among utilities.

From this directory, use Python 3.10 or later:

```sh
python3 analyze.py
python3 test_examples.py
```

Both commands run offline using committed metadata. `analyze.py` creates the [comparison matrix and coverage outputs](results/README.md), including two transparent bill calculations. The [data dictionary](DATA_DICTIONARY.md) defines every field. The [codebook](CODEBOOK.md) explains interpretation; the [methodological readings](../../01_Resources/42_Qualitative_Evidence/README.md) support the qualitative practices.

To retrieve the fixed public-source list:

```sh
python3 collect.py --download
python3 collect.py
```

The first command makes sequential requests and caches accessible documents with hashes and retrieval receipts. The second reprocesses the cache without network access. HTML extraction uses explicit article boundaries and excludes scripts and styles. PDF extraction, when used, requires `pypdf`; it removes repeated page furniture and retains page locators. Current verified runs use HTML renditions. The retrieval output and passage windows remain in ignored `.cache/`. Download failures remain unavailable; they never become zero-match documents. Inspect extracted boundaries and complete speaker turns before annotating. No API key, paid service, or external LLM upload is needed.

Direct automated retrieval of the Evergy and CenterPoint issuer-hosted PDFs and the SEC accounting disclosure returned HTTP 403. Separately accessible public ROIC transcript renditions were retrieved for both calls. Their selected passages were cross-checked against the issuer PDFs using the web reader. The PSEG passage was checked against its public transcript rendition and the regulator's related announcement; the original call recording was not independently transcribed. The accounting passage was checked with the web reader but remains absent from the machine-extracted corpus. The frozen snapshot records five successful document downloads and one unavailable document. A fresh collection writes a separate snapshot; it never silently replaces the committed release.

## Evidence and Course Coverage

M5 §5.27 supplies complete collection and analysis code, the qualitative procedure, and the source comparison. M6 §6.36 separates mechanism evidence from identification. M9 §9.33 uses the evidence in a stakeholder argument. Sessions 7 and 14 include the corresponding discussion. The [lab](../../07_Labs/Qualitative_Evidence/README.md) is optional ungraded practice.

The reviewed electricity paper itself allows cost recovery and reports positive residential spillovers. The case challenges categorical reassurance, residual causal attribution, and extrapolation beyond the study's 2020–2025 window. It does not claim that these disclosures overturn the historical coefficient. Most selected disclosures were made in 2026, after that window.

## Provenance and Rights

The instructor's existing analysis supplied research leads. The public adaptation uses independently checked third-party disclosures and original code and paraphrases; private notes and manuscripts are excluded. [sources.json](sources.json) identifies the primary documents and retrieval renditions. Full transcripts and lengthy extracts remain local because no redistribution permission was established. ## Source: 03_Data_and_Code/Utility_Cost_Recovery/CODEBOOK.md

# Qualitative Content Analysis of Cost Recovery

## Question and Analytical Approach

Under what conditions do utilities describe infrastructure investment reaching household charges, and which revenues or contractual protections may offset those charges? Use directed qualitative content analysis, beginning with recovery, allocation, timing, and offsets. Retain a category for material that does not fit. Hsieh and Shannon (2005, pp. 1281–1283) identify both the value of theoretically informed categories and the risk of favoring confirmatory evidence. Full references and links appear in the [methods guide](../../01_Resources/42_Qualitative_Evidence/README.md).

The prior expectation is that infrastructure costs may reach households. Record what would change that expectation: disallowed recovery, direct assignment to large loads, enforceable guarantees, or net bill reductions supported by an appropriate comparison. Assess these possibilities with the same care as passages describing higher charges. Commercial self-interest is a reason to inspect an assertion's basis; it does not establish that the assertion is false.

## Sampling and Context

This teaching selection follows known leads and includes documents with contrasting claims. It is neither a systematic review nor an independent test of a prespecified theory. Broader research should define utility jurisdictions, observation dates, document types, and inclusion rules before retrieval; include disconfirming cases; retain unavailable documents; and record how later sampling responds to unresolved explanations. Six documents do not establish thematic saturation.

Use a claim within a complete speaker turn or document paragraph as the coding unit. Read the surrounding discussion and the question that prompted an answer. Record the issuer, operating subsidiary, customer class, time horizon, units, speaker role, and prepared-remarks or Q&A context. A parent-company investor call does not identify every subsidiary's rate treatment. A syndicated transcript and its issuer PDF are renditions of the same event. The later Evergy release adds documentary specificity within the same corporate source family.

## Coding Rules

| Field | Inclusion Rule | Important Exclusion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `forecast` | A speaker expects a future outcome | A forecast does not establish realization |
| `request` | Recovery or rates are explicitly sought | Filing does not establish approval |
| `proposal` | An announced settlement or arrangement awaits the relevant disposition | Expected savings do not establish household receipts |
| `accounting_mechanism` | An accounting policy describes how costs enter recoverable amounts | Capitalization alone does not identify a residential allocation |
| `approved_price_illustration` | A regulator's announced auction result is translated into a stated-use bill | A bill illustration is distinct from observed household billing data |
| `regulator_explanation` | An agency identifies drivers or a pass-through arrangement | An explanation supplies no causal share without an identified comparison |

Code `direction` separately: increase, offset, mechanism, mixed, or unclear. Code the comparison, including current bills, a no-growth scenario, inflation, or another tariff. A claimed offset relative to higher counterfactual costs can coexist with a nominal bill increase. Retain both claims. Leave unidentified shares unspecified. The public codebook does not contain a label called “proof of harm.”

## Contextual Reading and Comparison

Read the entire selected document before relying on retrieved windows. Keyword searches prioritize passages; they can miss synonyms or match denials and analyst questions. Inspect a sample of unmatched passages and preserve reasons for exclusion. Record changes to definitions and revisit earlier coding after a revision. Complete source turns remain in the local cache; the public matrix supplies locators and original paraphrases.

Compare claims within an issuer before comparing issuers. Organize the matrix by mechanism, population, timing, evidence stage, and alternative explanation. This adapts the charting and within-case comparison described by Gale et al. (2013, stages 2–7). Similar words about “recovery” can concern gas infrastructure, electric supply procurement, or distribution construction. Preserve those differences before developing an explanatory theme.

For triangulation, identify what each source can establish. A call indicates an attributed position; a filing documents a request; an order establishes a regulatory disposition; tariffs and billing data support different outcome claims. Agreement between a company call and its own release does not supply independent corroboration. A regulator's illustration strengthens an institutional interpretation without identifying the contribution of a specific data center.

## Independent Review and Reflexivity

For a shared codebook exercise, two readers independently annotate the same complete passages before discussion. Keep their original records, compare disagreements, and document why a definition or interpretation changed. Use `data/reviewer_template.csv` for separate submissions. O'Connor and Joffe (2020, practical considerations) discuss when this procedure can clarify a coding frame. No independent human coding, agreement statistic, or accuracy estimate has been completed for this release.

The procedure fits a structured codebook analysis. Braun and Clarke (2021) explain why coding reliability is not a universal requirement for reflexive thematic analysis. An LLM can suggest passages or competing readings, with its prompt and model recorded. Repeated outputs from one model do not constitute independent human confirmation. Human agreement also cannot establish the truth of the underlying corporate claim.

Keep a reflexive memo stating the initial view, source-selection decisions, difficult interpretations, and revisions. SRQR (O'Brien et al., 2014, Table 1) supports transparent reporting of these choices and the connection between findings and empirical material. A quality checklist cannot replace substantive judgment.

## Stakeholders and Transferability

Investor calls reveal how management justifies investment and earnings expectations to capital providers. They provide limited access to household experience, ability to contest charges, or affordability tradeoffs. Extending the study to residents would require a separate sampling and consent process, alongside public comments, consumer-counsel filings, and billing evidence where appropriate. Do not infer residents' consent or silence from their absence in a corporate transcript.

The defensible result identifies documented mechanisms, competing claims, and the conditions under which an assurance needs further support. Generalization depends on institutional similarity and additional evidence. Counting selected adverse passages supplies no estimate of how often utilities transfer data-center costs to households.

## Source: 03_Data_and_Code/Utility_Cost_Recovery/DATA_DICTIONARY.md

# Data Dictionary

## Sources and Retrieval

`sources.json` has one row per selected document. `id` is the document key; `issuer` defines the source family; `date` is the publication or call date; `kind` distinguishes calls, announcements, and accounting disclosures. `url` is the requested retrieval address. `primary_url`, when present, identifies the original issuer-hosted transcript. `format`, `start_marker`, `end_marker`, and `identity_markers` govern extraction. `primary_locator`, `retrieval_note`, and `rights` record verification and permitted handling.

`data/retrieval_snapshot.json` contains the frozen executed collection. `source_id` joins the source roster. `status=ok` means the response passed identity and minimum-length checks; `unavailable` carries a reason and has no word or match counts. Successful rows record original and final URLs, HTTP status, UTC retrieval time, SHA-256 of raw bytes, byte length, extraction units (`pages`; one unit for HTML), candidate-window count, word count, and six regex-occurrence counts. The regexes are in `collect.py`. Counts refer to the extracted text, including analyst and management speech. They are not substantive claim labels or unique speakers. Adjacent candidate windows can overlap.

## Qualitative Annotations

`data/claims.json` contains ten purposeful claim records. `claim_id` is unique; `source_id` joins the source register. `speaker_context` and `locator` recover the relevant source passage. `stage` records epistemic or procedural status. `direction` separates increases, offsets, and mechanisms. `mechanism` names the proposed channel; `population` states the affected entity or class. `paraphrase` is original course wording, not a quotation. `counterevidence` preserves contextual qualifications and competing claims. `interpretation_limit` states the inference left unresolved. `annotation_status` identifies assistant source checking and pending independent human review. `historical_causal_effect_identified` is false for every selected claim.

`data/reviewer_template.csv` is a blank review form with claim ID, coder ID, stage, direction, source locator, reason, and unresolved question. Blank entries are uncompleted judgments, not agreement. Keep independent copies before discussing disagreements.

`data/excerpts.json` contains three short verbatim passages reproduced in the lecture notes. `source_id` joins the source register, `text` preserves the source wording, and `locator` identifies the relevant passage. Speaker, date, and contextual interpretation accompany each box in M5 §5.27.2. These excerpts are evidence of attributed statements; their wording does not establish whether a forecast subsequently occurred.

## Outputs

- `results/coverage.csv`: one row per selected source, with observed status, words, and recovery matches. Missing counts remain blank.
- `results/evidence_matrix.csv`: one row per coded claim, retaining all annotation fields, issuer family, date, and source URL. Related documents share a source family.
- `results/bill_illustrations.csv`: monthly usage in kWh, monthly dollar change, percentage where the original bill is supplied, annualized dollar change, and interpretation status. Annualization assumes twelve months of unchanged usage and rates. It does not measure realized yearly expenditure.
- `results/summary.json`: counts of selected documents, calls, source families, claims, stages, and directions. Denominators describe this teaching set only.

The one missing machine-retrieved accounting source is separately source-checked through the web reader. It can support a documented qualitative annotation, but it is excluded from computed text counts.

## Source: 03_Data_and_Code/Utility_Cost_Recovery/results/README.md

# Results and Interpretation

The selection has six documents, three earnings calls, five issuer families, and ten purposeful claim records. Five documents were downloaded and machine-extracted. Southern Company's accounting passage was checked through the web reader but remains unavailable to the executed downloader. Blank text counts for that source preserve the missing observation.

The comparison matrix retains five claims concerning increases, three concerning offsets, and two describing mechanisms. These counts follow the selected coding units. They are not frequencies among utilities or estimates of public sentiment. Related claims within one source provide context and should not be counted as independent confirmations.

The New Jersey regulator's fixed-use illustration for PSE&G changes from USD 155.84 to USD 182.71 per month at 650 kWh, a USD 26.87 change (17.24%). Holding that monthly comparison for twelve months gives USD 322.44. This arithmetic describes announced auction prices; later relief, other charges, and actual usage are outside the comparison. Evergy's proposed USD 17.25 monthly increase at 1,005 kWh would annualize to USD 207 under the same fixed-month assumption if approved. The release does not supply the original bill needed to compute a comparable percentage.

A recovery mechanism can operate while new-load revenue offsets part of its cost. Neither the proposed bill nor the auction illustration assigns a causal fraction to data centers. Wholesale capacity charges and recovery of construction investment are separate channels. Their relationship to historical effects requires matched project, tariff, and outcome evidence.

Regenerate the four files with `python3 analyze.py`. Definitions, source references, and verification status are in the parent folder. All computations use committed inputs; no paid service or external model is called.

# Utility Disclosures, Qualitative Evidence, and Affordability

A household advocate must respond to an assurance that data-center development creates little concern for electricity affordability. Use the [source register](../../03_Data_and_Code/Utility_Cost_Recovery/sources.json), [codebook](../../03_Data_and_Code/Utility_Cost_Recovery/CODEBOOK.md), and M5 §5.27 to identify what the evidence supports. This activity is optional ungraded practice; it establishes no assessment requirements.

## Define the Inquiry

Write the decision, population, time horizon, and comparison before reading the coded results. Record your prior expectation and the evidence that would change it. Explain why calls addressed to investors can reveal recovery plans while leaving household experience unobserved. Consult Hsieh and Shannon (2005) on directed content analysis and SRQR (O'Brien et al., 2014) on reporting context and reflexivity; full citations are in the [methods guide](../../01_Resources/42_Qualitative_Evidence/README.md).

## Retrieve and Assess Sources

Run the offline analysis first:

```sh
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Utility_Cost_Recovery/analyze.py
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Utility_Cost_Recovery/test_examples.py
```

The optional `collect.py --download` command retrieves the fixed public source list and creates local review windows. Inspect the article boundaries, issuer, date, speaker turn, and any preceding question. Compare a selected passage with the original issuer-hosted document. Record a failed retrieval as unavailable. Choose at least one unmatched passage to assess what the search missed; do not label the resulting check representative accuracy.

## Code Before Comparing

Two readers independently fill copies of `data/reviewer_template.csv` after reading the relevant source contexts. Preserve both records before discussion. Identify which disagreements concern the definition, the unit of text, or substantive interpretation; revise the codebook and revisit affected claims. If working alone, record that status and compare alternative readings without calling them independent coding. O'Connor and Joffe (2020) support deliberation about coding consistency; Braun and Clarke (2021) explain why this is not a universal requirement for every qualitative approach.

Build a comparison matrix with sources as rows and recovery, allocation, timing, and offsets as columns. Keep subsidiary and customer-class differences visible. This adapts the within-case and between-case comparisons of Gale et al. (2013). Explain why the Evergy call and release constitute one corporate source family and why a transcript mirror adds no independent observation.

## Test the Strongest Alternative Interpretation

Compare the investment-related increase with the offset in the Evergy and CenterPoint calls. For Evergy's later request, distinguish a lower requested amount than otherwise from a lower bill than today. For CenterPoint, identify the charge component and avoid treating a distribution revenue requirement as residential expenditure. Compare PSEG's explicit residential-bill statement with the New Jersey agency's multiple explanations and the absence of an estimated data-center share.

Prepare a short evidence table containing a supported statement, its strongest contrary or qualifying passage, and the remaining question. Propose the order, tariff, cost-allocation filing, or household outcome that would address that question. Select one conclusion you changed after examining counterevidence and explain the reason.

## Construct an Ought Argument

Use M9 §9.33 to formulate a recommendation. State a factual premise, a normative principle concerning burdens imposed on households, a feasible alternative, and the strongest objection. Explain why new costs and claimed offsets require transparent substantiation. Then consider the firm's objection that premature criticism could obstruct beneficial investment. Specify what evidence would justify modifying either recommendation.

The household advocate may criticize an overbroad assurance while accepting that the historical paper estimates a small average effect. A final answer must distinguish empirical contradiction, a competing mechanism, a scope problem, and a normative objection. It must also state whose experience the documents leave unrepresented.

## Evidence and the Proposed Action

Use [Evidence Standards and Reasonable Protection](../Evidence_Standards/README.md) to distinguish an inquiry, a temporary safeguard, and a remedy. Compare the consequences of false alarms and missed harm, defend the interests included in the analysis, and answer the strongest reasonable objection. The complete synthetic calculation appears in M6 §6.44; M9 §§9.55–9.59 connects the decision to disciplinary history and institutional standards.

## Source: 01_Resources/16_AI_Experimentation_and_Pricing/SCANLON_ASSESSMENT.md

# Pricing, Individual Reasons, and the Scope of Demand Models

## Empirical Claims and Normative Premises

A seller's ability to predict willingness to pay does not establish its authority to exploit the circumstances producing that willingness. The course compares the empirical representation, customer incidence, feasible alternatives, and reasons for adopting a pricing principle. The assessment concerns arguments and methods. Evidence of personal intentions, misconduct, exploitation of vulnerable individuals, or unlawful coordination would require additional facts.

| Work | Verified Setting and Contribution | Question for Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| *Personalized Pricing and Consumer Welfare* (Dubé and Misra, 2023), JPE 131(1) | Recruitment-service customers are employers; rich observed features predict demand parameters; empirical residual is logistic. June 2021 revision reports lower total customer surplus and a majority receiving lower prices. | Which circumstances, affected people, welfare assumptions, and alternatives determine whether the pricing rule is justifiable? |
| *Causal Alignment* (Angelopoulos et al., 2026), August version | Email subject lines, campaign click outcomes, human selection, and acceptability screening. | What customer outcomes and permissions remain outside click-based learning? This is not a field test of personalized prices. |
| *Robust A/B Decisions* (Farrell et al., 2026), 2609.07633v1 | Decisions under distributional ambiguity for a selected payoff. | Robustness to distribution change leaves the choice and justification of the payoff open. |
| *Coarse Personalization* (Zhang and Misra, 2025), 2204.05793v4 | A small number of segments can retain much of modeled personalization profit. | A short price menu does not itself establish morally appropriate classifications or customer control. |
| *Competitive Price Targeting with Smartphone Coupons* (Dubé et al., 2017), Marketing Science 36(6) | Randomized mobile promotions; historical visits and location; estimated static competitive pricing game. | Permission to use location history, inference from visits, competitive responses, and reasons beyond firm revenue. |

The detailed discussion and complete code are in [M9 §§9.34–9.39](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M09_Marketing_Dialectics.md). [M6 §6.37](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md) separates correct experimental estimation from a justified allocation of exposure. [Optional practice](../../07_Labs/Scanlon_Pricing/README.md) requires an objection, the strongest defense, and an explicit condition for revising the conclusion.

## Heterogeneity and Harm

M9 §§9.34.3–9.34.4 distinguish measurement quality, the worth of an objective, and the reasonableness of a governing principle. Unbiasedness and precision support reliance on factual estimates. Justifying an action also requires reasons concerning the people affected, their authority, burdens, and alternatives. A seller's profitable choice and a dependent customer's acceptance may each be instrumentally rational while the governing rule faces a strong reasonable objection. This is an application of the distinction in chapter 5, §2 (Scanlon, 1998); it does not reduce rationality in every sense to self-interest or treat every objection as decisive.

The strongest supported criticism is that a fitted representation can omit morally relevant mechanisms and that finite experimental support can leave welfare conclusions dependent on structure. Flexible heterogeneity does not generally imply downward-biased estimates of harm. The pricing paper itself finds a decline in total customer surplus. Its rich observed interactions also differ from learning all unobserved preferences: the residual remains uncertain to the firm.

The original course example uses two monotone demand completions with identical purchase probabilities at every tested price. Their candidate policies produce the same revenue increase but opposite aggregate surplus changes. The higher-price group loses in both. This is an identification counterexample, not evidence that either completion describes the original experiment. Under quasilinear utility, surplus differences are integrals between prices; arbitrary utility rescaling is not a valid critique of correctly computed money-metric compensating variation.

Welfare weights require separate interpretation. Lower modeled surplus does not establish lower income or weaker social advantage, and an enterprise's surplus is not a complete account of the people affected. The authors' inequality-sensitive welfare comparisons, fairness discussion, and recognition of limits are material responses to criticism. They still do not establish authorization, the absence of exploitation, or reasonable acceptability of the governing principle.

## Reading Locations

- [(Dubé and Misra, 2021)](https://www.nber.org/papers/w23775): June 2021 NBER revision, §§2.2–2.3, §§3–4, empirical model, validation experiment, welfare and conclusion. Local PDF pages 9–16, 25–28, 37–40 provide the model and central discussion; use printed headings because pagination differs from the [2023 publication](https://doi.org/10.1086/720793).
- [(Dubé et al., 2017)](https://www.fox.temple.edu/sites/fox/files/competitive-price-targeting-pub.pdf): published pp. 949–951 for sampling and measurement, pp. 963–966 for the equilibrium and Table 9. Table 9 was checked against the rendered page, then transcribed into an original JSON input.
- *What We Owe to Each Other* [(Scanlon, 1998, chapter 5 §§1–3)](https://e-edu.nbu.bg/pluginfile.php/314831/mod_resource/content/0/scanlon_5.1-3.pdf): reasons, reasonable rejection, and feasible principles. The water-owner example is on p. 192. Weak bargaining power does not determine the strength of a moral claim.
- [(Scanlon, 2009)](https://media.philosophy.ox.ac.uk/assets/pdf_file/0008/25856/Lecture_2.pdf): pp. 12–14 for the normative relation. The course distinguishes this metaethical account from its own assessment of analytical representation.
- [(Scanlon, 2009)](https://media.philosophy.ox.ac.uk/assets/pdf_file/0010/25858/Lecture_4.pdf): reflective equilibrium and justification. A defensible principle is tested against cases and objections.
- *Groundwork* [(Kant, 1785)](https://www.earlymoderntexts.com/assets/pdfs/kant1785.pdf): second section, Academy 4:421–430 for universalization and humanity. The linked Bennett text is a modernized rendering; Academy references identify the original passages. The course's hypothetical concealed-tracking maxim is an application, not an allegation about the experiment.
- [(Suikkanen, 2020)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10892-019-09282-6), *Journal of Ethics* 23, 77–98: §§1–5 distinguish ex ante and ex post objections and propose a synthesis. The course does not treat expected harm, maximin, or majority voting as a complete Scanlonian decision rule.

## Replication Access

The [JPE supplement](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/suppl/10.1086/720793/suppl_file/20190715data.zip) is publicly linked by the journal, but its download returned HTTP 403 on November 26, 2026. Its contents have not been verified.

The form states that files may be used to verify the paper's main results using the same data and models, restricts other reuse without permission, and specifies Marketing Science as the venue for a follow-up article documenting corrected central results. Download requires an email and acceptance of those terms. The course uses the executed published-table reconstruction. At the instructor's request, the form was not submitted and replication microdata were not downloaded.

# Antitrust Evidence and Reasons Owed to Customers

U.S. federal framework, checked November 26, 2026. The course application is hypothetical. Research methods and model predictions are not findings of unlawful conduct by the researchers or firms using their work.

## Match the Conduct to the Claim

| Issue | Legal Source and Scope | Evidence to Seek | Scanlonian Connection |
|---|---|---|---|
| Concerted restraint | [15 U.S.C. §1](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/15/1); [*Twombly*, 550 U.S. 544, 553–557 (2007)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/supct/html/05-1126.ZO.html) | Agreements, confidential input sharing, communications, recommendation commitments, independent overrides | People have reasons to object to coordinated removal of independent alternatives. Mere parallel behavior leaves agreement unresolved. |
| Monopolization | [*Trinko*, 540 U.S. 398, 407 (2004)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/02-682) | Monopoly power and a specified exclusionary mechanism | Unilateral exploitation can remain morally objectionable even where monopoly pricing alone is legally insufficient. |
| Price discrimination | [FTC Robinson–Patman guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/advice-guidance/competition-guidance/guide-antitrust-laws/price-discrimination-robinson-patman-violations) | Covered commodity sales, competitive injury, timing, cost justification and meeting-competition defenses | Equal prices and fair treatment are distinct questions; categorical statutory coverage does not exhaust a person's reasons. Recruitment services and admissions are not ordinary covered commodity sales. |
| Attributable injury | [*Brunswick*, 429 U.S. 477, 489 (1977)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/429/477) | Harm flowing from the anticompetitive aspect of the conduct | A justified remedy responds to an attributable burden while protecting against sanctions for unrelated losses. |
| Damages and class proof | [*Comcast*, 569 U.S. 27, 35–38 (2013)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/11-864) | A counterfactual and damages model matched to the accepted liability theory; heterogeneity and common proof | Accountability requires evidence of who is harmed; an aggregate change cannot answer every person's claim. |

These connections are philosophical interpretations of institutional reasons. Courts do not apply contractualism (Scanlon, 1998) as the governing antitrust test. Moral standing also extends to people who may lack a particular damages claim.

## Legal Literature

[Ezrachi and Stucke, “Artificial Intelligence & Collusion: When Computers Inhibit Competition,” 2017 University of Illinois Law Review 1775–1810](https://illinoislawreview.org/print/vol-2017-no-5/artificial-intelligence-collusion/) distinguishes a computer implementing an agreement, hub-and-spoke arrangements, predictable agents, and autonomous learning. Sections III–IV explain why the factual mechanism and legal response differ. The taxonomy motivates competing hypotheses; its discussion of enforcement gaps is not a rule that algorithmic price similarity establishes an agreement.

## RealPage: Allegations, Proposed Terms, and an Entered Judgment

The [DOJ case record](https://www.justice.gov/atr/case/us-and-plaintiff-states-v-realpage-inc) lists the November 24, 2025 [RealPage Competitive Impact Statement](https://www.justice.gov/atr/media/1419471/dl?inline=) and [proposed final judgment](https://www.justice.gov/atr/media/1419451/dl?inline=). The former describes allegations about competitors' nonpublic data and pricing alignment, and proposed remedies addressing inputs, training, software features, and monitoring. These documents are proposals and government allegations, not a trial finding. The same case page separately lists the [Greystar final judgment entered March 2, 2026](https://www.justice.gov/atr/media/1430091/dl?inline=). The recorded status is document-specific; the proposed RealPage terms are not described as a generally binding rule for other firms.

## Evidence and Counterfactuals

Use the pricing research to define customer segments, price support, substitution, rival responses, and welfare incidence. Then identify the conduct absent from the lawful counterfactual. A model trained on post-conduct customer states may preserve reduced alternatives in that counterfactual. A change in model fit does not resolve that causal issue. Demand experiments can inform price sensitivity while still leaving the effect of the alleged coordination unidentified.

The [worked Python example](../../03_Data_and_Code/AI_Experimentation_and_Pricing/compare_pricing_damages.py) assumes 92 actual units at $120 and a lawful price of $100 with 100 counterfactual units. It produces $1,840 in signed invoice differences and $1,040 in revenue growth. The eight excluded purchases require separate welfare evidence. The assumed benchmark is varied to show the sensitivity of the damages calculation. No actual firm, plaintiff class, violation, or empirically estimated damages is represented.

## A Defensible Ought Conclusion

Specify the affected person's burden, the institutional mechanism producing it, a feasible alternative, and the strongest objection to that alternative. A firm may reasonably invoke viability and useful forecasting. Those interests do not automatically justify a feature that suppresses independent discounts. If useful forecasting remains available without the restrictive feature, necessity is an empirical claim to test. Protecting customers against unjustified extraction and protecting defendants against unsupported attribution both matter to the justification of an enforcement institution.

See [M9 §§9.38–9.39](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M09_Marketing_Dialectics.md) for the detailed argument and complete code. This federal antitrust comparison does not determine separate consumer-protection, privacy, civil-rights, state-law, or non-U.S. claims.

## Source: 03_Data_and_Code/AI_Experimentation_and_Pricing/SCANLON_DATA_DICTIONARY.md

# Pricing Inputs and Denominators

## Synthetic Incidence and Experimental Exposure

`evaluate_pricing.py` supplies groups L (share 3/5; valuations uniform on $6–$10) and H (share 2/5; valuations uniform on $10–$30). Dollars refer to one purchase opportunity. Marginal cost and outside-option utility are zero. Groups reveal no demographic or social-advantage information.

`incidence.json` records each policy's prices, aggregate revenue/profit, customer surplus, and purchase shares. A `surplus_change_per_group_member` includes nonbuyers in that group; `population_surplus_contribution` additionally multiplies by its population share. Lost purchase shares compare the same valuations under both prices.

`experiment.json` uses invented assignment probabilities L=1/4 and H=3/4, compared with 1/2 in each group. Revenue outcomes include zeros. `ipw_policy_effect` is the eligible-population effect; `naive_difference` compares differently composed pooled arms. Expected loss is measured against always receiving control, with negative surplus changes truncated only when measuring loss rather than net gain. Exact expected cells have no empirical sampling uncertainty.

## Synthetic Demand Completions

`demand_completions.json` uses a separate population with weights L=3/5, H=2/5. Tested probabilities are L=(.9,.5,.1) and H=(.95,.8,.5) at $5,$10,$20. Each completion is a continuous monotone piecewise-linear curve, extended to probability one at zero and zero at $30. Candidate prices change from $10 for both groups to $5 for L and $20 for H. Areas under demand are money-metric surplus under the stated quasilinear assumptions. Both completions agree at all tested prices; no fitted sample or uncertainty estimate is implied.

## Published Competitive Payoffs

`competitive_payoffs.json` transcribes the published payoff table (Dubé et al., 2017, Table 9, p. 965). Rows select A's strategy, columns select B's, and each cell is [A revenue, B revenue]. Units are RMB expected revenue per messaged consumer. Decimal strings preserve the three-decimal rounding in the source. These are estimated model outputs, not observed individual transactions. The program derives pure-strategy best responses from the rounded entries and does not recover posterior uncertainty.

## Synthetic Invoice Comparison

`damages.json` uses one-period USD prices and identical service units. Its lawful counterfactual prices and quantities are assumed inputs. Signed invoice differences equal actual quantity times the paid-minus-counterfactual price; negative values are retained. This avoids silently declaring all transactions harmed. Revenue differences also reflect quantity changes. Lost consumer surplus and legal entitlement to recover damages are not identified by this accounting identity.

All exact fractional values are exported as an `exact` string and `decimal` numeric value. No model API, confidential customer record, or student information is used in these five programs.

## Source: 07_Labs/Scanlon_Pricing/README.md

# Pricing, Individual Reasons, and Antitrust Evidence

Public optional ungraded practice. No assignment deadline, grade weight, or assessment-specific AI permission is established by this exercise.

A manager wants to deploy personalized prices. A customer disputes the burden, and an investigator asks whether a shared pricing arrangement restricted competition. Use [M9 §§9.34–9.39](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M09_Marketing_Dialectics.md), [M6 §6.37](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md), and the [runnable examples](../../03_Data_and_Code/AI_Experimentation_and_Pricing/README.md).

1. Run the five programs and the tests. Explain why 60% benefiting can coexist with a large loss for H, and identify a profitable alternative. Keep group members, all eligible people, and actual purchasers as separate denominators.
2. Compare the demand completions. Explain why their likelihoods agree at tested prices and their welfare conclusions differ. Propose an additional price cell and explain which uncertainty it resolves. Identify the H-group conclusion that survives both completions.
3. Evaluate targeted experimental exposure. Derive the correctly weighted population effect and compare each group's expected burden. Defend a principle governing exposure; address a feasible less burdensome design and the ex ante/ex post objection.
4. Reconstruct the published payoff game (Dubé et al., 2017). Explain the small rounded deviation margin and what remains unknown about customer authority over location data. Specify a maxim before applying the humanity formulation (Kant, 1785). Do not infer concealment from an absent variable.
5. Build a hypothetical U.S. Section 1 case theory. State the alleged agreement, the facts needed to distinguish it from independent conduct, the lawful counterfactual, and the person whose injury follows from the restriction. Compute invoice differences under several benchmarks. Explain why the optimal monopoly price in another example is not automatically a lawful competitive benchmark.
6. Assume every factual estimate in the chosen example is unbiased and arbitrarily precise. Identify the reasons that still bear on whether the objective is worth pursuing. Distinguish an instrumentally rational choice from a reasonable principle, including a customer who accepts because alternatives are weak. Write a connected argument containing a supported factual premise, a defended normative principle, an ought conclusion, the strongest defense, and a condition for revision. Include a person excluded from buying and a person who would bear a mistaken enforcement decision. Explain where legal permission leaves a moral question unresolved.

A strong analysis can defend or reject a pricing practice. Its conclusion must survive the evidence and the strongest reasonable objection. Numerical optimization, a majority of winners, a sophisticated demand model, and a citation to legal doctrine each leave additional premises to defend.

Apply the same argument to dynamic-pricing communication and the data-center reassurance in M9 §§9.31–9.34. Identify the precise claim in each case, the affected people, the strongest objection, and a feasible response. Grant exact knowledge of the narrow measured effect and explain which moral or institutional questions remain.

For discussion, one person defends the objective and another represents an affected person with little bargaining power. Give both the same exact factual results. Identify whether the disagreement concerns a fact, a reason, or the relative strength of competing objections. Explain why actual acceptance, majority approval, and any single objection do not alone settle reasonableness.

AI assistance can help trace code, inspect denominators, and propose counterexamples. Check each legal quotation and claim against its primary source. Preserve actual terms, source versions, and execution status. Never invent empirical consent, a conspiracy, a damages estimate, or an author motive.

## Evidence and the Proposed Action

Use [Evidence Standards and Reasonable Protection](../Evidence_Standards/README.md) to distinguish an inquiry, a temporary safeguard, and a remedy. Compare the consequences of false alarms and missed harm, defend the interests included in the analysis, and answer the strongest reasonable objection. The complete synthetic calculation appears in M6 §6.44; M9 §§9.55–9.59 connects the decision to disciplinary history and institutional standards.

## Price Theory and Moral Permission

Read [M9 §§9.76–9.82](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M09_Marketing_Dialectics.md) and select an argument from the [13-source guide](../../01_Resources/50_Chicago_Price_Theory_and_Moral_Justification/README.md).

1. Run the [budget and compensation program](../../03_Data_and_Code/Price_Theory_and_Justification/README.md) and its verification. Explain why the willingness-to-pay ranking reverses and why the compensation policies have equal dollar totals but different resident burdens. State the units and the role of the synthetic assumptions.
2. Choose personalized pricing, online engagement, or infrastructure cost allocation. Write a conditional economic prediction and the additional premise needed for an ought conclusion. Distinguish profit, consumer surplus, total surplus, and actual compensation where relevant.
3. Grant the prediction for the sake of argument. Formulate the strongest objection from an affected person, including someone excluded from the transaction. Compare a feasible alternative and state the relevant Kantian duty or Scanlonian reason.
4. Present the strongest economic defense. Consider supply incentives, resource costs, information, interim losses, and unintended incidence. Explain which evidence could defeat your own criticism.
5. Distinguish a moral violation under established premises from an unverified empirical allegation and from a legal violation. Do not infer any of them from school affiliation or a method's name.

For the electricity case, identify the project commitment, the possible recovery path, the household outcome, and the resident's opportunity to participate. For engagement, distinguish intertemporal consistency from authority over a stopping purpose. For enforcement, compare an information request with a final penalty before defending the evidentiary threshold. These remain optional, ungraded activities.

# Logic and Analytical Arguments

A marketing recommendation combines evidence with premises about measurement, causal change, customer value, and acceptable conduct. These readings help students identify which premise supports each inference and what would justify revising it. [M1 §1.20](../../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md) introduces the five-step exercise. [M4 §4.29](../../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md), [M6 §6.38](../../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md), and [M9 §9.40](../../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M09_Marketing_Dialectics.md) develop valuation, identification, and ethical justification.

## Questions, Consequences, and Evidence

| Primary Source | Reviewed Material and Course Use |
| --- | --- |
| “The Erotetic Theory of Reasoning,” [(Koralus and Mascarenhas, 2013)](https://doi.org/10.1111/phpe.12029) | *Philosophical Perspectives* 27:312–365. The saved September 30 author manuscript, §§1–2, explains question-guided reasoning and illusory inferences. Students identify the question answered by a calculation and the broader question left open. [Oxford record and author manuscript](https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid%3Adb396f44-8020-4b8b-884b-a377bd8d191a). |
| “In What Sense (If Any) Is Logic Normative for Thought?” [(MacFarlane, 2004)](https://johnmacfarlane.net/normativity_of_logic.pdf) | Author manuscript, April 21, §§1–4. Distinguishes logical consequence from principles governing reasoning and belief. The course separates validity, acceptance of premises, and revision. |
| *Inquisitive Semantics* [(Ciardelli et al., 2018)](https://fdslive.oup.com/www.oup.com/academic/pdf/openaccess/9780198814788.pdf) | Oxford University Press, §§2.3–2.5, particularly pp. 24–25 and 31. Distinguishes information conveyed from issues raised. The course application examines which alternatives a managerial question includes. |
| “Causal Inference in Statistics: An Overview,” [(Pearl, 2009)](https://ftp.cs.ucla.edu/pub/stat_ser/r350.pdf) | *Statistics Surveys* 3:96–146, §§3.2.1–3.2.3. Separates the definition of an intervention from identification using observed distributions. Students specify the price rule, population, information, and preserved mechanisms. |

The [contractualist and stakeholder guide](../07_Stakeholders_and_Reasons/README.md) supplies the distinct normative foundation for justified principles, reasonable rejection, and affected people's reasons. Logical validity alone does not select a worthy objective. These applications do not attribute a marketing experiment, AI mechanism, or particular welfare model to the philosophers.

## Six Applications

1. **Compatibility and identification:** construct two models that fit the same historical law and disagree about the policy effect. State the evidence or restriction needed to distinguish them.
2. **Question formulation:** separate predicting acceptance, estimating an intervention effect, identifying a burden, and justifying a practice.
3. **Meaning and measurement:** preserve the distinction between purchase and consent, willingness to pay and benefit, unit price and household bill, and a formal option and an effective ability to use it.
4. **Counterfactual specification:** identify what changes and what remains fixed when pricing, disclosure, availability, or customer control changes.
5. **Valuation sensitivity:** hold purchase evidence and rank order fixed while varying independently supplied cardinal values. Attribute the resulting welfare change to that premise.
6. **Symmetric scrutiny:** require the criticism to preserve the source's actual claim and qualifications. An unsupported harmlessness inference leaves actual harm to be established separately.

## Practice and Reproduction

[Optional ungraded practice](../../../07_Labs/Philosophical_Arguments/README.md) includes a reusable argument record, worked pricing and electricity examples, an AI prompt, and a condition for revising each conclusion. [Two original Python programs](../../../03_Data_and_Code/Analytical_Arguments/README.md) use exact fractions and save complete numerical inputs and results. Five editable TikZ figures show historical equivalence, value-gap sensitivity, argument revision, epistemic limits, and ontological scope.

## Phenomena, Noumena, and Acknowledged Epistemic Limits

M9 §9.41 and the opening of M1 distinguish empirical representation, unmeasured empirical questions, and the practical standing of affected people. The negative concept of noumenon (Kant, 1781/1787) limits theoretical claims about things considered independently of the conditions of sensible cognition. The course separately draws on the practical account of respect (Kant, 1785) and the intelligible standpoint. Qualitative evidence and latent empirical variables remain within possible empirical inquiry.

- [*Critique of Pure Reason*, chapter on phenomena and noumena](../01_Kant_Primary_Texts/public_domain_texts/Kant_CritiqueOfPureReason_Meiklejohn1855.html), especially B306–B311. Read the existing Meiklejohn text and checked the A/B locators against the [Kemp Smith translation](https://humanum.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/humftp/E-text/Kant/cpr.kemp-smith/11ph-nou.htm).
- [*Groundwork*, sections II–III](../01_Kant_Primary_Texts/public_domain_texts/Kant_Groundwork_Abbott.html), humanity at 4:428–429 and the two standpoints at 4:451–453. Read the existing Abbott text. These practical arguments retain their distinct role from the first Critique's theoretical limit.

The “known to be the never known” is treated as an acknowledged epistemic limit whose scope requires justification. It differs from an unanticipated empirical issue. A statistical non-identification construction gives a conditional limit under a specified observable law; a changed design can remove that limit. Normative questions remain open to reasoned justification. They are not classified as permanently unknowable merely because statistics do not settle them.

## Ontology and Critiques of Empiricism

[M9 §§9.42–9.43](../../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M09_Marketing_Dialectics.md) assess specific interpretations along a five-position spectrum. It is an original teaching framework with no numerical distances or author rankings. A narrow, well-supported study can answer its stated question adequately. The criticism concerns an unsupported extension to persons, welfare, or permission.

# Analytical Arguments and Counterexamples

A retailer must decide whether a price change or a choice procedure benefits customers. These original synthetic examples separate agreement with observed purchases, identification of a policy effect, and the valuations needed for a welfare conclusion. [M1 §1.20](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M01_Marketing_Analytics_and_Python.md), [M4 §4.29](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M04_Conjoint_Segmentation_and_CLV.md), [M6 §6.38](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md), and [M9 §9.40](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M09_Marketing_Dialectics.md) connect the calculations to a five-step argument exercise.

## Inputs, Units, and Comparisons

`price_models.py` specifies a population with two equally common groups, one offer per customer, and prices of $10 or $20. Group A historically receives $10; group B receives $20. The price-response model assigns purchase probabilities of 0.8 and 0.4 at those prices to both groups. The selection model assigns 0.8 to group A and 0.4 to group B at either price. Both reproduce the complete historical joint distribution of group, price, and purchase. The counterfactual assigns one common price to the same population while preserving product, information, availability, and each model's response rule. Raising that common price from $10 to $20 changes population purchase probability by −40 or 0 percentage points. These are population constructions with no sampling error, fitted coefficients, or external data.

`valuation_sensitivity.py` compares purchase probabilities `(0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1)` with `(0.45, 0.2, 0.2, 0.15)`. Every customer purchases one of four products. Monetary consumption values are `(100, 2, 1, 0)` or `(100, 99, 98, 0)` dollars per customer. Both value systems have the same strict ranking and endpoints. Prices and other burdens are common across the two procedures; incremental procedural cost is zero. The consumption gains are +$4.80 and −$4.90 per customer. The program also accepts a separately specified incremental cost. These values are assumptions for a welfare comparison, not values estimated from purchases or inferred consent.

## Reproduction

Python 3.9 or later and its standard library are sufficient. No installation, network connection, credentials, or random seed is needed. From the repository root:

```sh
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Analytical_Arguments/price_models.py
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Analytical_Arguments/valuation_sensitivity.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s 03_Data_and_Code/Analytical_Arguments -p 'test_*.py'
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Analytical_Arguments/build_figures.py
python3 scripts/check_lecture_code.py
```

The complete analytical programs appear verbatim in M6 §6.38 and M4 §4.29. The figure builder reads the saved output tables and writes the two numerical TikZ sources. The separate argument diagram is editable directly. [Verification](VERIFICATION.md) records the checks run and their scope.

## Output Dictionary

| File in `results/` | Rows and Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `observed_purchase_law.csv` | Four group–purchase cells. `price_usd` is the historical offer; `population_mass` is the unconditional population probability. The common law applies to both models. |
| `conditional_purchase_rules.csv` | Eight model–group–price cells. `purchase_probability` is conditional on the named group and assigned price; `historically_observed` marks prices in each group's historical support. |
| `policy_effects.csv` | Two models. `purchase_at_10` and `purchase_at_20` average over equal group weights; `effect_pp` is 100 times the high-price probability minus the low-price probability. |
| `purchase_and_value_inputs.csv` | Four ordered products. Probabilities sum to one in each procedure. `cumulative_change_pp` is the alternative-minus-baseline change in probability of purchasing among the first k products, in percentage points. Two value columns give USD per purchased product. |
| `valuation_comparisons.csv` | Two value systems. Expected values, consumption gains, incremental costs, and net gains are USD per customer; gains subtract the baseline. |

## Interpretation and Provenance

The examples use exact rational arithmetic before CSV export. Observational equivalence is relative to the stated historical support. A new randomized comparison within groups would distinguish the two specified response models, subject to implementation and sampling uncertainty. A mathematical counterexample establishes failure of an entailment; it estimates neither the prevalence of the alternative mechanism nor actual consumer harm.

The valuation example separates an ordinal ranking from cardinal distances. Mixed cumulative purchase changes allow different signs under different ordered value systems. Customer permission, informed consent, and the reasons supporting a practice require their own evidence and argument.

The [reading guide](../../01_Resources/15_Marketing_Dialectics/08_Logic_and_Analytical_Arguments/README.md) attributes the philosophical and causal concepts. The numerical examples are original course constructions. No private research manuscript or third-party microdata is included. [Optional ungraded practice](../../07_Labs/Philosophical_Arguments/README.md) applies the same reasoning to pricing, mHealth, and electricity claims.

# Analytical Argument Record

## Claim and Question

Record the exact claim, source passage and locator, actor, proposed action, population, comparison, period, and units. State the question answered by the analysis and the question the decision requires. Define consequential terms such as benefit, consent, household cost, and permission.

## Ends, Representation, and Standing

State who selected the objective and what authority permits pursuing it. Identify unmeasured empirical questions and the evidence that could address them. Explain any Kantian limit on treating the empirical representation as complete. Defend the practical principle concerning the affected person's standing; identify which end the firm ought to pursue, constrain, or abandon.

## Ontological Scope and Epistemic Limit

Place the particular inference on the spectrum in M9 §9.42 and explain the placement through a source passage. Identify the object omitted or substituted and why it changes the decision. Classify the unresolved issue as an empirical gap, an unanticipated issue now recognized, a conditional identification limit, a Kantian theoretical limit, or a question of practical justification. State the scope and reason for any impossibility claim. Preserve the source's safeguards and welfare findings.

## Premises and Support

| Premise | Role: Factual, Measurement, Causal, or Normative | Evidence or Reason | Scope and Unresolved Issue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| State each premise separately. | Identify its role. | Give a source, calculation, assumption, or argument. | Name the condition affecting its use. |

## Counterexample and Missing Premise

Describe a case in which the stated premises hold and the conclusion fails. Check each premise against that case. Identify whether the construction is hypothetical or empirically supported, and identify the added premise that would exclude it. Explain why that premise deserves acceptance.

## Strongest Reply

State the strongest supported response to the criticism. Preserve the source's actual scope, positive findings, and qualifications. Check whether the objection establishes invalidity, unsupported interpretation, non-identification, a reporting inconsistency, or actual contrary evidence.

## Revised Conclusion and Further Evidence

State what the analysis supports and the evidence or reasons that would change the conclusion. For an ought claim, defend the normative principle, compare a feasible alternative, and assess affected people's reasons for rejecting each principle. Identify whose burdens or choices are missing from the analytical representation.

## AI Contributions and Independent Checks

When permitted by the applicable assessment rules, identify the assistant's contributions and the source checks, calculations, and counterexample checks completed independently. Record hypothetical outputs as hypothetical. This record establishes no course-wide permission to use AI.

An instructor deciding how to present an analytical argument needs to preserve its meaning while helping students investigate it independently. The course applications connect explanation, editable diagrams, executable calculations, and questions that expose unsupported premises.

# Learning Design and Outcome Comparisons

An instructor choosing a learning tool needs evidence about the outcome that matters and the contribution of each proposed feature. `learning_comparisons.py` contains two separate calculations: arithmetic using published rounded percentages and an original synthetic factorial example.

## Inputs and Interpretation

The 78% and 67% inputs come from [Google Research's announcement](https://research.google/blog/learn-your-way-reimagining-textbooks-with-generative-ai/). Their difference is 11 percentage points; the relative increase is 1100/67%, approximately 16.42%. These rounded summaries do not supply participant observations, sampling uncertainty, or a replication of the trial.

The four synthetic means are 60%, 66%, 68%, and 77%. Factor Q offers questions with feedback; factor F offers alternative representations. Population, source content, assessment, and study-time allowance remain common. Equal allocation defines the average main effects. The 17-point whole-package difference is consistent with multiple allocations of component effects. No student data, estimated treatment effect, or power calculation is contained in this construction.

## Run and Outputs

```sh
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Learning_Design/learning_comparisons.py
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Learning_Design/bill_identity.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s 03_Data_and_Code/Learning_Design -p 'test_*.py'
```

Python 3.10 or newer and its standard library are sufficient. The program has no random seed because it performs exact, deterministic arithmetic. CSV and JSON files under `results/` report the input cells and comparisons. Calculations use exact fractions; exports use decimal display values.

The [electricity page](../../08_Wiki/pilot/index.html) uses the existing [institutional bill table](../Statistical_Inference/results/institutional_bills.csv) and its [complete Python source](../Statistical_Inference/institutional_exposure.py). # Learning Tools, Evidence, and Independent Judgment

This optional, ungraded exercise asks whether an instructional change helps a student understand and challenge an analytical argument. It establishes no assignment requirement or course-wide AI permission.

## Predict and Explain

Open the [electricity case](../../08_Wiki/pilot/index.html), or use its [complete text](../../08_Wiki/pilot/LESSON.md). Predict the average monthly bill when realized revenue remains USD 100/MWh and average monthly usage rises from 1 to 1.1 MWh. Explain why the unit-price statistic alone leaves the bill unresolved. Reveal the calculation, then state what further evidence would support a causal claim about a data center.

Change the price to USD 125/MWh and usage to 0.8 MWh per account-month. State how this comparison changes the measurement claim. Separate an accounting identity, an attribution of a change, and a judgment about affordability. Write a condition under which the original study would support a narrower reassuring conclusion.

When an applicable assessment permits AI, ask an assistant to produce an alternative explanation from an identified course passage. Check whether it preserves units, assumptions, contrary findings, and the distinction between possible and established harm. Keep the original passage accessible. Judge the explanation by the reasoning it supports and the errors it introduces.

## Source: 08_Wiki/pilot/LESSON.md

# Price, Bills, and the Claim

By Nathan Yang

## The Decision

A utility reports an unchanged average electricity price. What would justify reassuring households about their bills? An average price describes revenue per unit sold. Average expenditure also depends on usage, while claims about harm require further premises about causation, affordability, and incidence.

This synthetic monthly comparison holds the same 1,000 accounts fixed. Baseline revenue is USD 100,000 and sales are 1,000 MWh. The average bill is USD 100 per account-month. These inputs illustrate an accounting relation and are not estimates from the data-center study.

## Predict and Calculate

Before calculating, predict whether the average bill rises, falls, or stays fixed when average realized price is USD 100/MWh and usage becomes 1.1 MWh per account-month. Explain the relation supporting the prediction.

The result is USD 110 per account-month, an increase of USD 10. Revenue and sales rise proportionately, keeping their ratio fixed. The [browser page](index.html) permits comparison prices from USD 0 to USD 400 per MWh and positive usage from 0.1 to 3 MWh per account-month. Its feedback compares the prediction with arithmetic and asks for separate evidence on attribution and affordability. Responses stay in the page, clear on reload, and are not graded or submitted.

| Synthetic Scenario | USD per MWh | MWh per Account-Month | USD per Account-Month |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | 100 | 1.0 | 100 |
| More Usage, Same Realized Price | 100 | 1.1 | 110 |
| Higher Realized Price, Less Usage | 125 | 0.8 | 100 |

## Inspect the Reasoning

**Intuition.** At the same realized price, greater usage raises expenditure. Different households can bear different burdens even when the account average is unchanged. Household resources and essential needs enter an affordability judgment.

**Equation.** Let R be monthly revenue in USD, S monthly sales in MWh, and N the matched account-month count for the same customer class. Then `(R/S) × (S/N) = R/N`: realized price times average usage equals average revenue per account-month. Use the same period, class, and accounting coverage throughout. A tariff's marginal rate may differ from realized revenue per MWh.

**Diagram.** Three boxes connect realized price, average usage, and the average bill. The default comparison holds price at 100 while usage rises from 1 to 1.1 and expenditure rises from 100 to 110. Attribution requires a counterfactual; affordability additionally requires household resources and needs. The account average leaves distributional incidence unresolved.

![Realized price times average usage equals the average bill; equal prices coexist with different bills.](../../06_Lecture_Notes/figures/M02_price_and_bill.png)

[Editable TikZ](../../06_Lecture_Notes/figures/M02_price_and_bill.tex).

**Python.** [bill_identity.py](../../03_Data_and_Code/Learning_Design/bill_identity.py) is a complete standard-library program that reads the [saved inputs](../../03_Data_and_Code/Statistical_Inference/results/institutional_bills.csv), verifies matched accounting, and writes [checked results](../../03_Data_and_Code/Learning_Design/results/bill_reference.csv). Its complete listing also appears in M2 §2.29 and the browser's Python view.

```sh
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Learning_Design/bill_identity.py
```

## Challenge the Claim

Suppose someone says, “The average price did not rise, so households experienced no harm.” Identify three separate premises.

- **Measurement:** the unit-price measure must connect to the expenditure or affordability claim. The synthetic identity demonstrates why that connection requires further quantities.
- **Causation:** the counterfactual concerns expenditure without the project. Higher observed bills alone leave attribution unresolved. Investment commitments, cost allocation, and timing require institutional evidence.
- **Justification:** the argument must defend which burdens count, whose reasons matter, and which protection is warranted. An average leaves both incidence and the practical principle open.

A defensible revision preserves the reported outcome, design, and uncertainty, then states what further evidence broader reassurance requires. The paper explicitly defines its realized-revenue measure. The criticism concerns extensions beyond the supported inference. Actual harm, contaminated controls, and deliberate deception each require separate evidence.

## Action While Evidence is Incomplete

A household representative may have credible evidence of a cost-recovery mechanism without a precise causal estimate of the bill effect. Seeking relevant records, using a temporary safeguard, and imposing a remedy are different actions. Their burdens and evidentiary requirements differ. Continued exposure also has consequences.

The following comparison uses hypothetical cases, with ten percent harmful and normal signals of means zero and two and variance one. Correct decisions have zero loss. When missed harm costs twenty comparable units and mistaken intervention costs one, the five-percent test gives expected loss 0.767 per case. The minimum-loss threshold gives 0.408. Reversing these costs changes the preferred signal cutoff from 0.601 to 3.596. These synthetic results describe a decision model; they estimate no actual household harm and supply no legal proof threshold.

![For fixed synthetic signals, expected loss changes with the action threshold. With missed harm twenty times as costly, the minimum lies below the conventional five-percent threshold.](../../06_Lecture_Notes/figures/M06_error_costs.png)

[Open figure at full size](../../06_Lecture_Notes/figures/M06_error_costs.png) or inspect its [editable TikZ](../../06_Lecture_Notes/figures/M06_error_costs.tex).

Explain which electricity records would justify an inquiry and what would justify a more restrictive action. State whose burdens enter the comparison, which normative premise supports protection, and what would change the conclusion. A p-value cannot be read as a posterior probability of harm. A sum of losses also leaves open whether a person's serious burden is reasonably justifiable.

The [complete Python example](../../03_Data_and_Code/Evidence_Standards/README.md), [M6 §§6.44–6.45](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M06_Causal_Inference_and_Experiments.md), [M9 §§9.56–9.59](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M09_Marketing_Dialectics.md), and [optional practice](../../07_Labs/Evidence_Standards/README.md) supply the derivation, sources, and opposing cost specification.

## Transfer the Argument

Consider an unchanged advertised subscription rate with payment for more months or services. Identify price, quantity, expenditure, and decision rights. State which accounting relations transfer and which contractual facts require new investigation.

A supported response preserves units and timing, separates possibilities from established effects, gives a credible comparison, and defends a normative premise when recommending action. It considers the strongest reply and identifies evidence or reasons for revision. A different policy conclusion can satisfy these criteria; agreement with the instructor alone supplies no substitute for reasons.

## Sources and Further Practice

- [Learning-design sources](../../01_Resources/43_AI_Augmented_Learning/README.md) and [optional practice](../../07_Labs/AI_Augmented_Learning/README.md).

This text preserves the substantive comparison, figure description, questions, feedback criteria, and source links. It does not reproduce the page's keyboard behavior or visual layout.

## The Object Behind the Estimate

A precise average unit price can leave household bills, future recovery, and authority to contest a decision unresolved. Ontological laziness occurs when a convenient variable is treated as an adequate account of the broader object without defending that substitution. The conceptual figure separates statistical performance for the chosen target from adequacy for the stated claim; it has no numerical scale.

![A precise answer can retain unjustified scope. Better estimation can leave the target and omitted relations unchanged.](../../06_Lecture_Notes/figures/M09_statistical_virtues_and_ontology.png)

The strongest reply is that every model abstracts and a carefully scoped estimate can provide useful evidence. The criticism must identify a consequential omission. Reassurance requires a supported bridge from the measured variable to the household burden. Use [M9 §§9.66–9.69](../../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M09_Marketing_Dialectics.md#966-statistical-virtues-and-ontological-laziness) and the [annotated sources](../../01_Resources/48_Statistical_Virtues_and_Ontology/README.md) to defend the criticism and a revised conclusion.

# Conflicts of Interest, Attention, and Consumer Authority

A commercial objective can influence the question an analyst asks before it influences an estimate. These readings distinguish opposing interests, duties governing judgment, disclosure, dependence, reward learning, and the justification of a proposed action. The course application is in M9 §§9.45–9.49, with connections in M1 §1.22, M7 §7.47, and M8 §8.33.

## Philosophy and Institutional Design

## Source: 03_Data_and_Code/Conflicts_of_Interest/README.md

# Conflicts of Interest and Engagement Objectives

A product team chooses a feed design while an analyst evaluates its consequences. The synthetic comparison separates commercial contribution, completion of user goals, regret, excess time, disclosure, and respect for a requested stopping point. M9 §§9.45–9.49 connects this choice to professional judgment, Kantian authority, Scanlonian reasons, and institutional safeguards.

## Inputs and Units

[policy_inputs.csv](policy_inputs.csv) contains eight constructed policy-by-group rows. Each policy applies to the same hypothetical population of 1,000 adult user-days: 800 leisure users and 200 users with a stated time limit. These are scenario aggregates, not observations from a platform or estimated treatment effects. No participant records, neural measurements, or clinical diagnoses are included.

| Field | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| `policy`, `group` | Feed design and user group defined before exposure |
| `n` | Number of user-days in the group under each scenario |
| `contribution_cents` | Total daily platform revenue less variable operating cost, in cents |
| `goals_completed` | Count meeting the purpose specified before the session |
| `regret_reports` | Count reporting unwanted use at a fixed next-day follow-up |
| `excess_minutes` | Sum of positive differences between actual and preselected intended minutes |
| `respects_stop` | Whether the design honors the user's stopping instruction; 1 means yes |
| `discloses_incentive` | Whether the design explains the commercial incentive; 1 means yes |

The finite feed contains stopping points. The endless feed continues despite the requested boundary. The disclosed version adds information while holding outcomes and control fixed as an explicit illustration. The user-controls design honors the boundary and allows deliberate continuation or revision. Excess minutes can follow an authorized revision of the initial intended duration; they alone do not establish overridden refusal. The data do not distinguish the effect of individual features within a design. The same people are represented in each scenario; the rows do not supply joint individual potential outcomes.

## Run and Outputs

Python 3.10 or later and its standard library are sufficient. No package installation, network access, AI service, or seed is required.

```bash
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Conflicts_of_Interest/evaluate_policies.py
python3 03_Data_and_Code/Conflicts_of_Interest/verify_policies.py
```

[evaluate_policies.py](evaluate_policies.py) validates unique rows, common population composition, counts, and units. It writes [policy_comparison.json](results/policy_comparison.json). The complete matching program appears in M9 §9.48. [verify_policies.py](verify_policies.py) checks independently calculated totals, group outcomes, equal-outcome disclosure scenarios, tied maximizers, weight sensitivity, and the separately imposed stopping condition.

## Interpretation

The endless design earns USD 0.314 per user-day, compared with USD 0.236 under user controls. Goal completion is 85.6% and 91.8%, respectively. Among time-limited users, regret is 45% under endless use and 5% under user controls. Those figures follow from constructed inputs; they provide no prevalence estimate of problematic social-media use.

The program's regret penalty is a hypothetical managerial weight in USD per report. It has no standing as a measure of consumer welfare, a clinical threshold, a legal rule, or the reasonable-rejection test (Scanlon, 1998). A separately defended obligation to honor stopping instructions restricts the feasible policies before commercial ranking. The proposed restriction is a moral premise in this example. The code checks its consequences without establishing its justification.

[Optional practice](../../07_Labs/Conflicts_of_Interest/README.md) asks students to defend and challenge the premise. Execution and checks are recorded in [VERIFICATION.md](VERIFICATION.md).
